1:
the Thousand Maws of Toto-Rak

Toto-Rak was redesigned in patch 6.1, replacing much of its cramped layout with a more open environment.

## Entrance to the second boss
Spiderweb barriers open automatically after all nearby enemies are defeated.

## First and second bosses: Coeurl O' Nine Tails
The boss does not cast attacks, but continually poisons nearby players. Ranged players should stand away; heal the tank and melee players through the damage. The second boss summons two adds at approximately half health. The tank should pick them up.

## Second boss to the final boss
Follow the straight passage. The sticky floor sound near the boss room is a remnant of the old slowing floors.

## Final boss: Graffias
Avoid the green floor around the room: it inflicts Heavy. Dodge the marked attacks. After the web cast, a random player's position receives a web-covered fleshy pod. Move outside its yellow circle before it bursts and poisons nearby players.

When Graffias exposes its tail, the tail embeds in the floor and creates a large poisonous puddle. Avoid the puddle and immediately switch to Graffias's tail. If left alive, it creates more poison and reduces the available safe space. The tank should collect the adds. If an add attacks the healer, bring it toward the tank.
2:
the Tam-Tara Deepcroft

The route is mostly linear, with a few side passages. Tanks should watch the map.

## Altars
Kill the enemies guarding each altar, then the voidsent that appears. Remove the orb to proceed.

Between the second and third altars, walking instead of running can avoid attracting the blind crabs. They are spread out, so this approach is not commonly used. There is also a sharp turn that can be easy to miss: check the map.

The third altar is sealed. Continue to the deepest room, defeat its enemies, and obtain the rosary to remove the barrier.

## Final boss: Galvanth the Dominator
When the boss tethers to adds, it becomes invulnerable. DPS should kill the tethered adds first, then resume attacking the boss.
3:
Copperbell Mines

This early dungeon is straightforward. Pick up firesand, place it at a blasting point, then activate the blasting device by right-clicking it. Duty Support NPCs may not board lifts immediately; they will teleport to you afterward.

## Entrance to the first boss
Defeat the entrance enemies and collect the key. Only one player needs to collect it; the others can wait at the door. After descending, smaller pulls are safe. An experienced, well-geared party can instead let the tank run to the last room without the healer healing or DPS attacking: approximately half the enemies will leash, leaving fewer than ten to defeat. Collect the firesand and operate the devices afterward.

## First boss: Kottos
The long jumping attack leaves a safe section of the arena: move there. Immediately afterward, dodge the frontal cone. The heavy strike against the tank is a tankbuster; use mitigation.

## First boss to the second boss
After the next lift, both side rooms contain a blasting bomb that drops firesand. The other enemies have short leash ranges. The tank can gather a room, kill its bomb, collect the firesand, then move to the other room to let the previous enemies reset.

## Second boss: Ichorous Ire
Move out of the circular AoE placed beneath a random player. After the splitting cast, smaller slimes appear and use point-blank AoEs: avoid them. The heavy strike against the tank requires mitigation.

## Second boss to the final boss
The route has dense groups of enemies, but no additional special mechanic.

## Final boss: Gyges the Great
For the large sweeping attack, stand beneath the boss; the rest of the arena is hit. For the following crushing attack, move away and find the safe area. Continue dodging its frontal cone and mitigate its tankbuster.
4:
Sastasha

Use AoE attacks to establish enmity on the numerous enemies. The winding route is not difficult, but tanks should watch the map. NPCs outside the entrance appear again in early duties and later quests.

## Entrance to the first boss
Check the Bloody Memo in the dead-end side room. Its hint identifies the correct coral switch: a blue sea means blue, wine means red, and vegetables mean green. One DPS or a confident healer can check it and tell the tank the color.

Clams are invulnerable while closed and summon wisps when open. Wisps do little damage individually, but can accumulate. With newcomers, prioritize the clams; tanks with weaker gear should mark targets.

## First boss: Chopper
Dodge the marked attacks.

## Captain Madison encounters
Fight the adds before Madison. After his first retreat, enter the large room and head to the captain's quarters. Defeat the nearby enemies for the key, then defeat the enemies inside to obtain the next door key.

For the exploration achievement, you can return to unvisited side rooms after clearing the bosses. During the second Madison encounter, again prioritize his initial adds. The tank should pick up the dogs he summons; finish Madison, then clean up the dogs.

## Route to the final boss
After leaving the cave, follow the left wall to avoid enemies on the right.

## Final boss: Denn the Orcatoothed
Tank the boss near the center. Bubbles appear at the grates around the arena; the healer and ranged DPS can interact with them to prevent adds from emerging. A well-geared group may ignore these adds while the healer sustains the party and kites them.
5:
the Aurum Vale

Enemies hit hard and several mechanics inflict damage over time. Tanks and healers should be cautious.

## Entrance to the first boss
Follow the left wall. Avoid gold pools and vents. Keep pulls small, ideally no more than four enemies; the toads are particularly dangerous.

## First boss: Locksmith
The boss repeatedly applies a stacking party-wide damage-over-time debuff. Eat a Morbol Fruit to clear it at two or three stacks. More than three can become difficult to heal; players who keep four or five stacks place considerable strain on the healer.

## Route to the second boss
Kill the buds before they hatch. Avoid the morbols' Bad Breath attack.

## Second boss: Coincounter
For the frontal sweep, the tank should move through the boss. For the large point-blank swing, everyone should move out; a tank caught in it needs strong mitigation, and non-tanks can be killed outright. Dodge the frontal line attack. The broad, approximately 270-degree eye attack can be avoided under the boss, behind it, or at long range, and can also be stunned. If hit, the healer should heal or cleanse the resulting damage-over-time effect.

When the message says Coincounter is reconsidering its target, enmity resets. The tank must quickly establish enmity again.

## Route to the final boss
Defeat the two large morbols to open the way. Buds can be ignored if you do not trigger their hatching.

## Final boss: Miser's Mistress
Eat fruit at two stacks of the boss's debuff. At certain HP thresholds it moves and scatters buds: kill them before they hatch. A caster limit break can hit both the second group of buds and the boss.
6:
Haukke Manor

The layout can be confusing. Prepare interrupts and stuns: tanks have Interject and Low Blow, melee DPS have Leg Sweep, and physical ranged DPS have Head Graze.

## Entrance to the first boss
Go left and collect the small key in the first room. Manor Maidservants cast Dark Mist; interrupt or stun it and defeat them promptly. Otherwise, leave its area to avoid Terror, which prevents movement.

## First boss: Manor Claviger
Its targeted void-fire cast has a flashing cast bar and can be interrupted with Interject or Head Graze. Dark Mist has a nonflashing cast bar, so normal interrupts do not work, but Low Blow or Leg Sweep can stun it. Repeated stuns build resistance; use them carefully.

## Route to the second boss
Collect the key, turn back, and open the door. You can jump down instead of taking the stairs. Follow the left side clockwise without entering every small room. Strong parties can handle this route in two pulls. The boss-room key is in the last room, the wine cellar.

## Second boss: Manor Jester and Manor Steward
Defeat both enemies. The Jester uses frequent, strong elemental attacks and can gain an ice-spike effect that may reflect physical damage. The Steward uses a point-blank AoE that can be stunned. Weaker parties should prioritize the Jester; the tank can mark the kill order.

## Route to the final boss
Collect the note, then use the aetherial flow to return to the entrance. Go upstairs. For the exploration achievement, return after the boss to visit the remaining side room.

## Final boss: Lady Amandine
She summons several types of adds:
- A large eye in the center casts a petrifying gaze. Everyone must face away from the eye.
- When a maidservant appears, immediately switch targets and kill it; otherwise it gives the boss Stoneskin.
- An eye at the edge appears alongside the boss's charming mist. As soon as Charm wears off, turn away from the eye to avoid petrification.
7:
Halatali

Watch the map at junctions. After a boss, use the aetherial flow to reach the next section; you cannot simply walk there.

## Entrance to the first boss
Follow the left route and avoid bomb explosions.

## First boss: Firemane
Adds periodically move from the surrounding braziers toward the central fire. Reaching it triggers party-wide damage. Strong groups can largely ignore them, but weaker groups should kill the last, more dangerous add in each line.

## Route to the second boss
Use the aetherial flow inside the fire. Operate every chain winch along the route; each may reveal enemies or treasure. Do not activate them too quickly if the tank has weak gear. All chains must be opened to reach the next boss.

## Second boss: Thunderclap Guivre
The tank should pull it from the pool onto the slope at the edge. It periodically returns to the center, becomes invulnerable, and summons adds. Avoid the electrified water. Kill the adds, then resume attacking the boss; repeat as necessary.

## Final boss: Tangata
Tank it near the center, away from the add spawn points. As with Firemane, earlier adds in a line may be ignored while the final dangerous one is killed. When a fire circle appears under Tangata, it becomes invulnerable. Switch to the fire elementals near the entrance; defeating them removes the circle and lets you attack Tangata again.
8:
Brayflox's Longstop

The open layout allows some enemies to be avoided. Healers should prepare Esuna: many enemies inflict cleansable Poison.

## Entrance to the first boss
Follow the stream upstream, then take the left fork toward Brayflox's watch hut. Speak to the goblin for the key and continue through the woods to the first boss.

## First boss: Great Yellow Pelican
Three adds begin beside the boss; a ranged DPS can handle them, otherwise another party member should assist. Further waves appear during the fight. If the boss remains above approximately 30% HP, kill the adds; below that, the party can focus the boss. The tank can mark the intended kill order.

## Route to the second boss
After the short tunnel, take the second turn on the left across the small bridge toward the rear of the refuge. You do not need to climb the steps.

## Second boss: Inferno Drake
Brayflox periodically taunts the boss and runs toward a random player. Do not panic if the boss follows her toward you; it returns after its attack. Another drake joins later. Maintain damage-over-time effects on both if useful; the tank should mark the order, with the new drake first recommended.

## Route to the third boss
Follow the right-hand boundary around the broad lake.

## Third boss: Hellbender
Dodge marked attacks. When a player is trapped in a bubble, DPS should switch to it immediately. If it is not destroyed promptly, the healer must prepare for heavy party damage. At low boss HP, Aiatar briefly joins the fight; damage it until it retreats.

## Final boss: Aiatar
After the toxic-slime cast, move away from the expanding puddles, using the gaps between puddles at the arena edge. Later, two consecutive sets appear: dodge the first explosion, then move to the center for the second. Its venom bite is a tankbuster; mitigate it and use Esuna to remove Poison.
9:
the Sunken Temple of Qarn

Some mechanics can kill you outright if mishandled.

## Entrance to the first boss
Follow the right wall to avoid some enemies. Underground, prioritize Temple Bees. Their Final Sting deals approximately 80% of their current target's HP, ignoring mitigation. Kill bees individually unless the party has very strong AoE damage. Stuns or knockbacks can interrupt the cast, but the bee immediately recasts. If it will finish, the healer should prepare a large heal as the cast approaches halfway. Do not chase the retreating stone face in the first room into the next group of bees.

## First boss: Teratotaur
Mortal Ray applies Doom to the whole party. Step on a glowing floor tile to remove it. The active tile changes, so check your status bar or party list to confirm Doom is gone; otherwise you die when it expires. Prioritize the bees the boss summons.

## Route to the second boss
Kill stone faces on their pressure plates. A plate stops glowing when the enemy is positioned correctly. If killed elsewhere, the face revives. The second pair and their two plates can be skipped if you do not want the optional final-room mechanisms; they leash in the next room.

Walk past the blind crabs before the second boss, but avoid the wandering soul, which still detects walking players. Resume running inside the boss room.

## Second boss: Temple Guardian
Destroy the golem's soulstone first to remove the boss's damage reduction. The tank should maintain enmity while the healer watches random attacks on other players. Repeat the soulstone phases, generally two or three times. A melee limit break can be used on the vulnerable boss.

## Route to the final boss
Another group of blind crabs can be bypassed by walking. Optional doors upstairs require the matching named statues; wrong choices spawn enemies. Opening them is not mandatory.

At the scales, place the Flame of Magic on the left and Fruit of Knowledge on the right, then activate them. Correct placement opens a left-hand secret passage with three chests, also needed for the exploration achievement. Incorrect placement spawns enemies. Skip the scales if you did not collect both statues.

## Final boss: Adjudicator
Kill summoned stone faces on their plates; a DPS can handle them without the tank if capable. One type of staff fires blue line AoEs and may be ignored. The other creates a black rectangular enclosure: a DPS must enter it to damage and destroy the staff before it explodes for party-wide damage. The tank need not handle the staffs.
10:
the Wanderer's Palace

Large Tonberry Stalkers pursue the party and inflict extremely heavy damage.

## Entrance to the first boss
Ignore the opening tonberries and adventurers. The route is commonly pulled in three groups. When the warning announces a stalker, a large tonberry appears at the entrance. It moves slowly. If the party's damage is low, tank enemies in a corner of the last room and have everyone stay there. If spotted, run; once a player enters the boss room, the stalker retreats.

## First boss: Keeper of Halidom
Dodge the marked attacks.

## Route to the second boss
Collect lantern oil from defeated tonberries to operate the devices. In the large room beyond the first door, three stalkers patrol. Activate the first device ahead, then move toward the corridor area and kill enemies in a corner before activating the second. Watch the next stalker's position; hide against the corner if it approaches. Its sides and rear are safe.

After descending, fight near the third device from the corner of the platform by the doorway. For the fourth device, the tank can Sprint to draw enemies and the stalker away while the healer follows and operates it. The DPS waiting by the doorway should enter the newly opened corridor immediately, then help kill the remaining enemies there.

## Second boss: Giant Bavarois
Switch to the summoned adds promptly.

## Route to the final boss
Clear the first enemy group before stepping onto the platform, which triggers another stalker. Before the final door, fight in the corner on the corridor side and wait for the stalker to leave before opening it.

## Final boss: Tonberry King
With sufficient damage, focus the boss. If party damage is low, ranged players should kill the small tonberries before returning to the boss. Do not attack the medium-sized tonberries.
11:
the Stone Vigil

Enemies hit hard. Tanks and healers should check their gear; the source recommends an average item level above 40. Tanks should know their mitigation tools.

## Entrance to the first boss
Wyverns drop down and breathe fire at certain passage locations. Do not stop pulls beneath them. Follow the tank closely or remain approximately 10 yalms behind, and avoid breaking the healer's line of sight.

## First boss: Chudo-Yudo
When it leaves the tank and moves toward an edge to cast its sweeping attack, follow and move to its side or rear. Later it repeats the attack twice; watch both attacks and heal the damage. Its fast frontal fire breath targets the tank, so other players should not stand beside the tank.

## Route to the second boss
Watch junctions and patrols. Ice sprites can deal strong critical hits; heal accordingly.

## Second boss: Koshchei
Its whirlwind cast creates three or four tornadoes at the far end. They travel toward the exit and disappear. Watch their order and movement and cross through safe gaps. Touching one stuns and knocks you back.

## Route to the final boss
The enemies continue to deal heavy damage.

## Final boss: Isgebind
Keep non-tanks away from its frontal breath. Its party-wide frost attack hits hard; party mitigation helps. At HP thresholds, it takes flight and dives across approximately one third of the arena. Move away from the frosted strip. From the second flight phase onward, it first places two sets of ice circles on the party and then dives twice. Avoid both sets of attacks.
12:
Cutter's Cry

## Entrance to the first boss
Defeat the ants, then use the quicksand to proceed.

## First boss: Myrmidon Princess
At an HP threshold, ants join the fight. The healer can draw their enmity with healing and kite them in a broad circle. Keep the Myrmidon Marshal away from the boss.

## Route to the second boss
The party can run straight through without attacking enemies and quickly use the next quicksand passage. Someone familiar with the route can lead. If this is difficult, clear enemies normally. Chests on either side of the lake can contain special crafting materials.

## Second boss: Giant Tunnel Worm
Cleanse the Sludge debuff with Esuna. When the boss burrows, it either travels in a line and emerges at the edge, or creates quicksand pulling everyone toward the center before emerging. Both emergence attacks damage nearby players. Move toward the edge when it burrows: avoid the traveling line, or keep running outward against the quicksand pull.

## Route to the final boss
There are minor side passages, but no special mechanic.

## Final boss: Chimera
For The Dragon's Voice, or the message that its dragon head glows, move close to the boss. For The Ram's Voice, or the message that its ram head glows, move away. A targeted player may also be pursued by a lightning orb: kite it away from the party and return after it stops moving.
13:
Dzemael Darkhold

The opening has several branches. Large pulls require confident tanks and healers.

## Entrance to the first boss
Experienced groups can pull to the final room and use its back-right corner to break ranged enemies' line of sight. Otherwise, stop in the glowing floor areas. Stand in the blue-ring terminals to complete their countdowns; multiple players speed them up. Terminals 3 and 4 in the room are sufficient to open the way. Clear enemies before operating terminals outside the glowing floor: the roaming boss uses heavy party-wide attacks.

## First boss: All-seeing Eye
The boss is invulnerable outside the glowing crystal areas. Tank both the boss and yourself inside one, and keep the rest of the party there too for Crystal Veil's damage reduction. When the crystal light begins to fade, find the next active area. The party can take heavy damage while moving. With low damage, defeat the summoned adds before resuming the boss; strong groups may ignore them.

## Route to the second boss
After teleporting, follow the main crystal-lined route instead of side passages. Crystals explode when approached. Toads can pull players into their vicinity, potentially combining the pull with a crystal explosion. Tanks and healers should stay alert.

## Second boss
Dodge the marked attacks.

## Route to the final boss
Defeat all enemies in the first hall, then complete the terminal countdowns. Nearby crystals explode, so heal players operating the terminals. Several players together can shorten a countdown.

## Final boss: Batraal
When the boss tethers to a crystal and becomes invulnerable, destroy the crystal. The tank can assist; attacking the boss during this phase is ineffective. After all three crystals are destroyed, avoid puddles placed beneath targeted players. Keep the boss positioned so melee players can reach its rear and sides. It also uses an untelegraphed close-range AoE: ranged players should keep their distance and the healer should watch melee HP.
14:
Amdapor Keep

Large pulls benefit from frequent interrupts and stuns, including Interject, Low Blow and Leg Sweep.

## Entrance to the first boss
Interrupt the enemies casting voidsent summons. Pull to the first dullahan or beyond the first room as appropriate, interrupting another summoner on the way. Follow the right side through the courtyard and stop to kill the summoner near the door. Careful positioning avoids some dullahans; those you engage hit hard.

## First boss: Psycheflayer
The initial enemy summons the boss with a cast you cannot interrupt; defeat it. Kill the smaller golems that appear. Later a large golem uses a very broad AoE; move the party toward the entrance. A sufficiently strong party can instead finish the boss before the large golem becomes a problem.

## Route to the second boss
There are many enemies, including statues that activate. Experienced tanks may divide the route into three or four pulls; watch the map and adjust to party capability.

## Second boss: Demon Wall
It attacks random party members regardless of enmity. The center floor darkens first, then the sides: leave each marked area. After the side attacks, return to the center for Repel. Remaining at either side during the knockback can push you off the platform.

## Route to the final boss
Gather the additional ranged enemies carefully.

## Final boss: Anantaboga
Its tail sweep has a very large area. The tank should orient it sideways, and melee players seeking rear positionals can bait the sweep before moving behind. When it casts Imminent Catastrophe, everyone must hide behind a statue. Kill the adds if needed; very strong groups may ignore them.
15:
Castrum Meridianum

This main scenario dungeon includes unskippable cutscenes.

## Entrance to the first boss
Continue forward and defeat every enemy to open the security barriers.

## First boss: Black Eft
The high-powered magitek laser targets a random player's direction without a ground telegraph. Avoid the boss's front. The tank should gather its numerous adds; use AoE attacks to clear them.

## Route to the second boss
Use the refuse chute shown in the cutscene. After loading, go upstairs and follow the right wall. Turn left at the blockade with two magitek vanguards to enter the fifth restricted area.

## Second boss: Magitek Vanguard F-1
When a bomb-drop proximity marker appears, move away: damage falls with distance. Dodge the other telegraphed attacks. Mitigate the drill tankbuster.

## Route to the final boss
Take the right fork. Defeat the three enemies, then continue as the NPC breaks the wall. Follow the NPC's magitek armor.

## Final boss: Livia sas Junius
Her opening attack deals party-wide damage, followed by a tankbuster. For the inside-then-outside attack, begin outside the central circle, then move into the center as soon as it resolves.

During her blade sequence she cannot be attacked. Watch the AoEs and avoid them in their appearance order. If necessary, taking one hit is preferable to overlapping several.

Her bomb drops combine ordinary AoEs with proximity markers. Dodge the ordinary attacks first, then choose a safe position: with two bomb markers, use the outer edge midway around the arena from the pair, forming an isosceles triangle with their positions; with four markers, use the center.

After Magitek Enhancement, she repeatedly deals party-wide damage. Keep the party healed and finish the fight quickly.
16:
the Praetorium

Follow the party through the routes and avoid attacks; recovering after dying midway can be awkward. Cid later gives you a magitek armor mount through the story.

## Entrance to the first boss
Clear the enemies and activate the magitek terminal. After teleporting, follow the enemy-lined route; defeating each group opens the next passage or teleporter.

## First boss: Mark II Magitek Colossus
Dodge the marked attacks.

## Magitek armor section
After the first boss and teleporter, right-click the magitek armor to board it and proceed through the broken wall. Its first action, Magitek Cannon, deals 4,500 damage in a targeted area; the second, Magitek Photon Stream, deals 3,000 damage in a 10-yalm line. The first is generally sufficient. Stay away from the prototype arms' sweeping knockbacks. Destroy the reinforced wall to reach Nero.

## Second boss: Nero tol Scaeva
Keep away from the plasma floor at the arena edge. Gather for his stack marker. For the knockback, move toward its origin so the arrows push you safely outward.

When a Magitek Death Claw appears and tethers to someone, that player should keep moving away to lengthen the tether while the others destroy the claw. Dodge the other attacks and maintain party HP.

## Final boss: Gaius van Baelsar
After Nero, activate the terminal for the cutscene. Blue crosses appear in front of Gaius and fire line attacks; move to either side. Gather for the stack marker. Clones later appear along the north edge and repeat the cross-shaped tells into line attacks: stand between their lanes.

Circular AoEs appear in sequence and resolve in the same order. Start in unmarked ground or a later circle, then move into the first circles after they explode. Attacks can follow closely together; keep the party healed.

At very low HP, four phantoms appear while Gaius's energy gauge rises. Kill all four while dodging attacks. Defeating them or filling the gauge triggers party-wide damage; a full gauge makes the attack lethal. Destroy the phantoms before it reaches 100.
17:
Pharos Sirius

Frequent AoEs make this dungeon demanding for healers.

## Entrance to the first boss
Strong parties can pull the first floor together; otherwise split the groups.

## First boss: Symond the Unsinkable
Avoid the arena AoEs. Hounds apply a debuff with each hit; three stacks cause an explosion. Strong parties may focus the boss, but this puts heavy pressure on healing. Weaker parties should kill the hounds first and dodge carefully. Prepare party-wide healing.

## Route to the second boss
Aether crystals fall onto the spiral stairs. If the tank cannot sustain a large pull, stop at a landing. Prioritize the large corrupted sprite.

## Second boss: Zu
Do not attack the eggs around the arena. When they hatch, prioritize male birds, identifiable by their tethers. When Zu takes flight, everyone should move away from the tank, who should keep running around the arena until Zu lands.

## Route to the final boss
On the fourth floor, the healer or a DPS can turn off the aether-emission devices. Touching an aether sphere causes a small, relatively weak explosion. Kill slimes promptly before they summon smaller ones.

## Third boss: Tyrant
Attack the boss directly; the source lists no additional required mechanic.

## Final boss: Siren
Tank Siren near the center, facing away from the party. Prioritize crawling adds, which immobilize players. Her song gives a random player a lethal debuff: heal that player to full HP to remove it. When she takes flight, watch for either a line dive or an area attack and heal the damage.
18:
Copperbell Mines (Hard)

Damage is higher than in the normal dungeon.

## Entrance to the first boss
Only attempt a full pull after descending if both tank and healer are confident and party damage is strong. Otherwise stop at the first and third rock barriers and clear enemies.

## First boss: Hecatoncheir Mastermind
Strong groups may defeat it near the entrance. Otherwise, move it away from burning floor. Prioritize bombs appearing at the opposite end: after a timer or on touching fire, they explode for heavy party-wide damage. Other adds can wait.

## Second boss: Gogmagolem and Biggy
A DPS should activate the device, collect a bomb, and place it beneath Gogmagolem. Because the boss moves, wait until the warning says approximately five seconds remain before placing it. The healer should watch party HP while others kill fire sprites and other adds. After enough explosions, Biggy dismounts: everyone should focus him. Most groups can finish before the next bomb explodes.

## Route to the final boss
Clear the numerous enemy groups at a manageable pace.

## Final boss: Ouranos
Tank the boss at the edge. The healer or an assigned DPS should locate the crystals. When the sandworm begins searching for food, carry a crystal onto the sandy ground. Otherwise it pulls everyone into the center and deals heavy damage. Prioritize adds attacking the crystal carrier.
19:
Haukke Manor (Hard)

## Entrance to the first boss
Collect keys and open the doors along the route.

## First boss: Manor Jester
The boss summons adds and later revives defeated ones. If four revive together, they combine. Strong groups can finish before the second revival; otherwise the tank should separate the adds and kill them in different locations.

## Route to the second boss
Blue-patterned floor sections deal damage. Pull enemies to safe areas such as stair corners.

## Second boss: Ash
Avoid its frontal cleave and broad blue floor AoEs. Targeted players leave spinning blades on the floor; do not stand in them. Later it summons adds and uses random black-hole attacks. Use damage cooldowns to finish quickly, ideally as the adds appear; a melee limit break can help.

## Route to the final boss
Follow the circuit of rooms. The tank should collect enemies emerging from side rooms.

## Final boss: Halicarnassus
She summons adds, consumes them, and casts Blood Rain. Its damage depends on the consumed add's remaining HP: immediately switch to adds and lower their HP. The second wave has two adds and she chooses randomly, so damage both. If she consumes one above half HP, prepare emergency healing or a possible wipe.

Excessive boss damage can force consumption early, while an add is still at full HP. Stop attacking the boss when necessary. If you trigger this accidentally, a tank limit break may protect the party.
20:
Brayflox's Longstop (Hard)

## Entrance to the first boss
Experienced parties commonly pull to the bridge; new tanks should use smaller pulls.

## First boss: Illuminati Commander
Tethers can be passed to another player. Avoid the cross-shaped bomb attacks.

## Route to the second boss
The next large pull hurts more than the opening. Attempt it only with strong AoE damage and confident tank/healer play. Kill all Illuminati goblins so the rescued goblins open the secret route. Gliders attack random players regardless of enmity; heal those targets.

## Second boss: Magitek Vangob G-III
Dodge the marked attacks, particularly the path of its targeted charge.

## Route to the final boss
Take the bridge on the right, then head left to the far end. Stack in the corner to avoid attracting the coeurls.

## Final boss: Gobmachine G-VI
When it circles the arena, kill the adds. After they die, it throws bombs into the arena. Hit the bombs with attacks to knock them to the edge; an AoE attack is convenient. Focus the large bomb that appears afterward. Alternatively, a melee limit break at approximately 12–13% boss HP can finish the fight.
21:
Halatali (Hard)

Speak to the NPCs near gates to open them.

## Entrance to the first boss
Enter through the right gate. Falling hammers apply vulnerability to players and enemies alike. Tank enemies beneath the dark hammer-impact marks while standing outside the impact yourself. You can jump through the gap in the bridge railing on the enemy-free side. A ranged DPS or healer can fetch the three distant enemies while the tank gathers the pull with mitigation.

## First boss: Pyracmon
For the frontal sweep, move to the side; for the point-blank swing, move away. When the arena turns blue, operate the device behind the boss. Its tethered mammet stops and creates a blue circle. Everyone must enter it to gain the protection needed for the following swing. Avoid the boss's frontal glare. Afterward, go upstairs behind the boss and speak to the NPC to move on.

## Route to the second boss
Avoid the bears' and coeurls' frontal cleaves.

## Second boss: Catoblepas
When its eyes glow yellow during Demon Eye, each player should use a dark orb at the edge. When the Tainted Eye appears, kill it quickly: the boss repeatedly deals AoE damage and applies vulnerability while it remains alive. Strong groups may finish the boss instead.

## Route to the final boss
The route is long but has few enemies. Prioritize the central enemy in each group.

## Final encounter: Mumuepo the Beholden
First defeat the four gladiators. One lancer pursues a random player; stay calm while the tank holds the others. The recommended priority is the healer or lancer, then the archer, then the swordsman. Exact order is flexible, but the healer and archer are dangerous and the lancer can heavily damage its target.

Mumuepo then appears with a beast. The tank should hold both while DPS prioritize Mumuepo. He binds two random players and casts a broad attack. A free player must interact with the restraint device to release them; there is ample time. After defeating Mumuepo, finish the beast.
22:
the Lost City of Amdapor

## Entrance to the first boss
Gremlins apply Misery, increasing damage taken. Another player can remove it with the Comfort emote; you cannot remove your own this way. Kill mold-covered trees quickly before they summon additional enemies, and consider prioritizing moths that heal other enemies. Of paired chests at the first doorway, the right one is real; the other contains a mimic.

## First boss: Decaying Gourmand
When it swallows a player, the remaining party must attack its mouth to free them. Dodge the other attacks and cleanse Poison.

## Route to the second boss
At the next paired chests, the left one is real. You can cross the yellow hazardous ground, but do not stop to fight on it because it continuously deals damage.

## Second boss: Arioch
Begin with the adds. Their death spray applies a scale-powder effect to players in front, attracting Arioch but also increasing damage taken. The tank should receive it; other players can attack from behind or at range. Maintain the effect by defeating another add shortly before it expires, or focus on adds throughout. If another player also gains the effect, the tank can gain an additional stack to regain the boss's attention.

## Route to the final boss
Destroy towers before attacking enemies tethered to them. Weaker parties can pull the untethered enemies away first, then have ranged DPS destroy the towers. Stronger parties can gather the group with mitigation and destroy towers immediately. The four enemies in the later four-tower group are ranged, so gather them carefully.

## Final boss: Diabolos
Eight doors form four matching pairs. Their symbols appear at the pull and disappear shortly afterward. The three non-tanks should mark matching doors using target markers. Interrupt Nightmare or the party falls asleep. Keep away from the orb placed on a random player.

Approximately halfway through Ruinous Omen, open two matching doors to avoid its heavy damage. Well-geared groups may attempt to finish without doors while preparing emergency healing; most groups can finish after using one pair.
23:
Hullbreaker Isle

## Entrance to the first boss
Avoid bear traps, which immobilize you. Follow the right wall to bypass some enemies, but kill every monkey to unlock the first boss. Prioritize bees: at low HP, Final Sting deals fixed damage equal to approximately 80% of the target's maximum HP, ignoring mitigation.

## First boss: Sasquatch
Kill the adds; the tank need not collect them. When the hunger warning appears, the boss repeatedly deals increasingly heavy party damage. Interact with an edge tree to drop bananas and let the boss eat. It is vulnerable while using these attacks, so the healer can decide when to provide bananas according to party damage and HP. If healing remains manageable, continue attacking; others should handle the tree if the healer does not.

## Route to the second boss
Open all chests. Some contain mimics, and chests or mimics provide the three tablets needed for the door. The river's nanka can be bypassed by walking, dismissing pets and passing behind it. Cross the river for the chest, then cross back and follow its left side.

## Second boss: Sjoorm
Keep away from bubbles until needed, since they pull you inside. On every second burrow, a large whirlpool appears: enter a bubble to survive it. Missing the bubble causes heavy damage; heal accordingly.

## Route to the final boss
After jumping down, walking with pets dismissed can bypass the first crabs. Hidden jellyfish appear immediately afterward. Defeat them and take the far-right route; its chest can contain a minion. Watch for large birds joining the fight.

## Final boss: Kraken
Defeat the arms, two per island for eight total. Prioritize the two tentacles when they appear because they grab and throw players. A player marked with a green meteor should jump to an empty neighboring island. Wait until the marker disappears and a whirlpool forms, then return: the whirlpool explodes across its island. If a whirlpool is accidentally placed on the party's island, leave immediately.
24:
the Tam-Tara Deepcroft (Hard)

Fast target switching is important. The scattered notes and cutscenes contain horror imagery.

## Entrance to the first boss
Defeat the smaller enemies tethered to large enemies before attacking the large ones.

## First boss: Liavinne
When a player is marked and adds appear, do not attack the adds or use AoE attacks. Gather together and let the boss's targeted attack kill them.

## Route to the second boss
Clear all three side rooms. Opening a coffin spawns a Dantalion that stuns the opener and casts an AoE. Another player with a stun should stop the cast. Without a melee DPS, the healer can open the coffin while the tank stuns the enemy.

## Second boss: Spare Body
Black holes spawn small orbs that players must intercept. Without mitigation, take no more than two before healing. Larger orbs should be intercepted by two or three players together. Avoid the puddles; the tank should position the boss to leave DPS room to attack. The central NPC must survive, so heal them if their HP becomes low.

## Route to the final boss
Enemies stand immediately outside the room; let the tank lead. Defeat the tethered adds at the final altar and avoid the aether explosions.

## Final boss: Avere Bravearm
Stay out of the dark central floor, which deals continuous damage. Quickly destroy the adds approaching from the edge. Each one reaching the center lights a rune; four or five lit runes make a wipe likely. The healer should judge the healing required from the number of active runes.
25:
the Stone Vigil (Hard)

Watch the bosses' animations as well as their casts.

## Entrance to the first boss
Mitigate large pulls and keep the tank healed.

## First boss: Gorynich
When it moves to an edge, follow and stand at its side or rear to avoid a powerful 90-degree frontal attack. Immediately switch to summoned dragons and keep the boss away from them: their deaths strengthen nearby allies, which becomes dangerous at high stacks.

## Route to the second boss
Prioritize heretics casting Dragon's Blood. Stuns delay the cast, but they restart immediately afterward. If it completes, they transform into dragons that use powerful AoEs.

## Second boss: Cuca Fera
Each player operates a cannon at one of the four corners. Stop attacking the boss when it hardens, because it reflects cannon fire. Use the cannons to kill adds near party members. Save the cannon's second action, the lightning shot, to interrupt the boss's party-wide attack.

## Route to the final boss
Again stun and focus heretics casting Dragon's Blood.

## Final boss: Giruveganaus
It ignores enmity. Watch its posture: raised arms signal a frontal cleave; a raised rear signals a rear cleave; both arms held to the chest signal a frontal fireball line; one arm across its chest with its body turned sideways signals a charge. It also breathes fire forward without a telegraph. Attack from the sides and keep ranged players out of its front. A second dragon joins later: finish one before the other.
26:
the Sunken Temple of Qarn (Hard)

## Entrance to the first boss
After collecting the first stone, strong groups can have the tank gather enemies while the healer opens the door. Place enemies on the spikes beyond the door, but keep players off them: spikes damage enemies and apply vulnerability.

## First boss: Damaged Adjudicator
Focus whichever body part begins glowing; mark it for newcomers if helpful. Targeted players should move away before dropping a stone orb that repeatedly deals AoE damage. Leave quicksand quickly or you will sink and die.

## Route to the second boss
Follow the left wall after leaving the room, giving the far corner a little extra clearance before descending. Prioritize hands that grab players and snakes that petrify them.

## Second boss: Sabotender Emperatriz
Focus-target and mark the boss among the many cactuars. Deal enough damage to interrupt 100,000 Needles; completion wipes the party. When its guard appears with a large protective effect, the boss becomes invulnerable while continuing the cast. Kill the guard first, then damage the boss to interrupt; use a limit break if necessary. Other adds disappear when the boss dies and can be ignored if the tank and healer can cope.

## Route to the final boss
After the final enemy group, activate the two side devices, then the central one.

## Final boss: Vicegerent to the Warden
Tank it near the center and watch the arena edges. Mummies emerge from coffins and move in straight lines; touching them applies a curse stack. Dodge the boss's frontal line attack aimed at a random player.

A tethered player should keep running around the arena. Tanks or melee DPS can stun the boss, allowing for diminishing stun effectiveness. If the boss catches its target, it repeatedly applies curse stacks. Four stacks imprison the player and turn them into a mummy that crosses the arena diagonally, spreading stacks to anyone hit. If the tank is imprisoned, the boss attacks the next player on the enmity list.
27:
Snowcloak

## Entrance to the first boss
Large pulls are possible with appropriate tank mitigation.

## First boss: Wandil
A blizzard follows the snowstorm cast after approximately two to four seconds. Keep moving or jumping to avoid gaining stacks. Kill frost bombs promptly, as their explosions also add stacks. After the tundra attack, avoid the blue floor at the edge. Four stacks freeze you and deal damage over time.

## Route to the second boss
Do not stop in the blizzard areas, which inflict Frostbite. Ice sprites are awkward to gather; move a little farther to group them. A full pull is not recommended because damage is high.

## Second boss: Yeti
A party-wide blizzard creates snowballs. The boss blows snow onto some balls, enlarging them; stay away from the large balls and their ensuing AoEs. For the nested inside/outside circles, begin outside the inner attack, then move inward once its telegraph disappears to avoid the outer attack.

## Route to the final boss
Glacial sprites self-destruct after being hit a few times; gather them and avoid their explosions. Stun and focus heretics casting Dragon's Blood. They resume casting after the stun; completion transforms them into dragons with strong AoEs.

## Final boss: Fenrir
Hide behind an icicle for Lunar Cry. From the second set onward, three icicles glow purple and only one remains normal: hide behind the normal one. Immediately leave it after the boss's attack or its explosion freezes you. For the targeted cone roar, move out of the boss's front. Heal frozen players carefully.
28:
Sastasha (Hard)

The bosses deal frequent damage and require timely cleansing.

## Entrance to the first boss
After clearing the opening enemies, operate the device to drain the seawater.

## First boss: Karlabos
Spread slightly. Its spit applies a cleansable Slime debuff with damage over time and a movement penalty; cleanse affected players promptly and heal them to full.

With lower damage, Tail Screw may occur and remove approximately 90% of a player's HP. Stun the first cast with the tank. Later the tank is stunned first, so a melee DPS should stun Tail Screw. The stun-target marker can be passed, but passing it risks additional spit or other damage. Regardless of the planned stun, the healer should begin a large heal around halfway through the cast in case it completes. Slime and Tail Screw together can be particularly dangerous.

## Route to the second boss
Two rooms contain an enemy healed by approaching bubbles. Strong DPS can focus the main enemy. Otherwise, ranged DPS should destroy bubbles while melee attack it. With weak damage, first kill the other two enemies so the healer can help attack, then handle the main enemy. The tank and healer should choose and mark the order.

## Second boss: Captain Madison
He continually summons adds and charges players. When he marks someone and begins shooting, everyone must focus the boss to stop the shooting before the target dies. His adds hit relatively softly; prioritize crawling adds that immobilize players.

## Route to the final boss
The large enemy before the door summons many adds. Stay together so the tank can gather them. A paladin can protect the healer; otherwise maintain AoE enmity. A ranged limit break may help.

## Final boss: Kraken
Kill the arms, then attack the body. Tentacles can be ignored, but move away from their grabs. The tank can stand deep beside the boss to reduce incoming damage. The room is large and players move frequently, so the healer must check that party heals actually reach their targets.
29:
Amdapor Keep (Hard)

## Entrance to the first boss
Prioritize stationary plants and trees blocking the route, which otherwise keep summoning enemies. Vines strike the ground; tank enemies beneath the strikes to apply vulnerability, while players avoid them. Grouping the scattered enemies this way requires care.

## First boss: Anchag
Do not face the boss toward a statue. When targeted by its damaging tether, hide behind a statue until the tether ends; tanks can be selected too. If a statue breaks or the player does not hide, heavy healing is required. For the targeted charge, move close beneath the boss to minimize the charge distance.

## Route to the second boss
Vine strikes can again apply vulnerability to enemies.

## Second boss: Boogyman
When it disappears, destroy a light orb and step into its light to gain the illumination effect. Approach the invisible boss; when your effect expires, the explosion reveals it.

Two groups of adds are revived. Prioritize the largest add in the second group, whose self-destruct cast deals extremely heavy party-wide damage. Heal continuously if it is not stopped in time. Below half HP, a boss double appears. Reveal and defeat one at a time rather than both together.

## Route to the final boss
Gather everyone before the tank activates the device in the wall-surrounded room. Defeat all enemy waves before the countdown expires or the party wipes.

## Final boss: Ferdiad
Avoid the frontal cleave. When the boss returns to the center and tethers to adds, kill every tethered add to stop its central AoE from expanding, then wait safely outside. Destroy the slime restraining a player; the trapped player can attack it too. Dodge the remaining attacks.
30:
the Wanderer's Palace (Hard)

Well-geared, experienced groups can make large pulls. With newcomers or weak play, use smaller ones.

## First boss: Frumious Koheel Ja
Dodge the marked attacks and promptly destroy spears it throws onto the floor; they repeatedly deal party-wide damage.

## Route to the second boss
Pull all enemies out of the red circles around battle standards before fighting them, as those areas strengthen the enemies.

## Second boss: Slithy Zolool Ja
Four totem colors correspond to Toad, damage up, reduced fire resistance, and Heavy. Colors are randomized per duty but remain consistent within the fight. Test the first set to identify damage up; the color absent from that set is the Toad totem. From the second set onward, DPS should collect every damage-up totem before the boss absorbs them and gains the effect itself. A player turned into a toad can touch the Toad totem to return to normal.

## Route to the final boss
Rescue every tonberry after defeating enemies so they blast open the exit. Kill the large slime first to remove the poison floor.

## Final boss: Manxome Molaa Ja Ja
Tank it in the center. Move it away from battle standards, but destroy sacred idols. Heal a player with Doom to full HP to remove it before the timer expires. Stay fairly close to the boss to make its broad 120-degree AoEs easier to avoid.
31:
the Great Gubal Library

## Entrance to the first boss
Well-geared groups can divide the opening enemies into two or three pulls; less confident tanks can pull fewer at a time.

## First boss: Demon Tome
Leave the black floor lines. When the book closes, run around a side to its back. Frozen floor makes movement slide, so control your direction carefully.

## Route to the second boss
Prioritize Page 64 enemies dropping from above: they tether to a player and repeatedly use line AoEs. Another player can remove Misery with the Comfort emote.

## Second boss: Byblos
For the tethered charge and knockback, the target can stand close: the damage does not decrease with distance.

When the boss returns to the center and becomes invulnerable, defeat the Page 64 enemies. A resulting orb tethers to a player, who must lead it through the boss to remove invulnerability. The orb disappears if it hits another player or a tornado. Others should clear the path; they can remove tornadoes by touching them.

## Route to the final boss
Prioritize the owl enemy immediately.

## Final boss: Everliving Bibliotaph
Six purple circles surround the arena. A red-marked player should place their orb at the edge between two circles; it damages its surroundings.

When the boss returns to the center and casts, stand in the glowing circles to extinguish their lights. The first set has six circles requiring one player each. The second has four circles requiring two players simultaneously. The third has two circles requiring three players simultaneously. Entering separately does not satisfy the multi-player circles.
32:
the Keeper of the Lake

Frequent ground attacks can make casting difficult.

## Entrance to the first boss
Large pulls are possible; no special route mechanic is listed.

## First boss: Einhander
Birds drop fuel tanks as the boss moves to an edge. With six tanks, its line attack ignites two first, then the remaining four. Avoid the tanks that glow red. With five tanks and a proximity marker, find the gap without a tank along the arena edge.

## Route to the second boss
Destroy the magitek barrier generator before attacking the large soldier. Large pulls are generally possible. Face the soldier's frontal cone away from the party.

## Second boss: Magitek Gunship
It moves to an edge and throws fire circles in its facing direction: watch where it points. During the flamethrower, the tank can move to its side and return after it finishes.

## Route to the final boss
Randomly targeted aerial AoEs also damage enemies. Stacking can bait them onto the pull, but this is optional. Keep wyvern cleaves away from the party.

## Final boss: Midgardsormr
Avoid both red and blue ground attacks. For expanding concentric red rings, begin in the second ring, then move into the center after the first circle explodes. Attack summoned enemies and dodge the remaining mechanics.
33:
Neverreap

The route crosses separate islands, so simply looking at the map is not always enough.

## Entrance to the first boss
Speak to the opening NPC for the item that activates the first transport. On each island, defeat all enemies to activate the totem's whirlwind transport. Dodge the route's tornadoes; the source mentions a possible safe position around X:10.6,Y:15.3, but treats it as unreliable.

## First boss: Nunyenunc
Dodge attacks and defeat adds. When mist hides the boss, locate its shadow. Stand inside the shadow's circle to damage it and quickly clear the mist.

## Route to the second boss
Without strong AoE damage, consider fighting the bees two at a time.

## Second boss: Canu Vanu
It places a totem at a targeted player, then marks a large black circle. Carry any totems out of the circle. Healers and ranged DPS can handle these first; tanks can assist with nearby totems. If a totem remains inside when the cast ends and becomes active, prioritize destroying it.

Do not linger inside the water spouts; they deal damage.

## Final boss: Waukkeon
Falling from the arena is fatal and prevents recovery. A bubble-marked player can stand beneath the boss to make the bubble easy to destroy with AoE.

At an HP threshold, the boss becomes invulnerable, moves around, and summons three wind sprites. Kill the sprites while avoiding the boss and tornadoes. Once all sprites die, the boss immediately becomes targetable and casts a knockback. Stand close to it with more than half the arena behind you so you are not blown off. Repeat the sequence as necessary, typically three times.
34:
the Vault

Boss damage is high and all four players must handle mechanics. Keep party HP healthy.

Enemies run in from a distance. Let the tank lead.

## First boss: Ser Adelphel
Heal the player he immobilizes and repeatedly strikes. His dashes leave light orbs that later explode; approximately five yalms of separation is enough. If necessary, taking one orb is survivable, but three will kill a non-tank.

Gather melee enemies onto ranged ones, or use a corner to break line of sight and draw the ranged enemies in. Mitigate while doing so: breaking enemy line of sight may also block the healer. Large enemies hit particularly hard.

Tank it centrally and face its cleave away. Targeted line attacks create black holes at their ends. Approaching a black hole creates a tether and sustained damage too heavy to heal through; stay away. Non-tanks can align the attacks to put the holes together. Before the knockback, adjust your position so you are not pushed toward a hole.

A lone caster near the end retreats to the center and summons four gargoyles. The tank should collect them.

## Final boss: Ser Charibert
Dodge the fire circles, which may be faint. Two tethered players must move in opposite directions to break their tether; one player moving alone is insufficient. Dodge its attacks. Remaining close, even as ranged, makes its successive quarter-arena AoEs easier to avoid.

Large birdmen use painful tornado AoEs. Prioritize chimeras: move away for their ice roar and close for their lightning roar.

the Dusk Vigil

New level-51 players may have weak gear or unfamiliar rotations, so large pulls are not recommended by this guide.

The route is linear and has no special mechanic.

A marked player is stunned, followed by one of two attacks. For the inhaling attack, everyone else should move to the sides or rear to avoid its frontal pull and knockback. Many apparently fallen enemies stand up as you pass. Watch the ground and expect heavy incoming damage.

37:
Sohm Al

Frequent movement demands quick reactions. Duty Support provides additional story context for a first run.

## Entrance to the first boss
Prioritize the poisonous plants that scatter pollen clumps. The healer or ranged DPS can destroy remaining clumps after the pull. Exploding near one applies Poison, and several together become dangerous.

Keep its frontal cleave away from the party. A marked player should avoid the hornets' direction while everyone else kills the hornets. The marked player is drawn beneath the boss and can leave afterward. Do not let the boss inhale hornets, which grants it damage up.

## Route to the second boss
Large dragons descend unexpectedly and may chase the healer before appearing on the enemy list: the tank should watch for them. Ice pillars melt into sprites that later self-destruct. You can ignore both and dodge the final AoE, or pull enemies back into the passage to simplify the situation.

Stay fairly close to dodge its very long cone attacks, but avoid its cleaving front. For slime attacks, red means share damage and blue means take the hit alone. In the second slime set, quickly kill the green slime: its explosion is likely to wipe the party.

## Route to the final boss
Expect more fire dragons, ice dragons and ice pillars. Dodge their attacks.

Tank it centrally, keeping its front toward the outside when moving. Dodge the many AoEs from Chaos Blast; overlapping two is usually lethal. Green-comet targets should move away from the party to the edge, place their comets, then return quickly. Comets may be placed together; their proximity damage is greatly reduced once you are more than half an arena away.

During the central wing phase, attack both wings while avoiding repeated AoEs. Red-meteor targets should place them at the edge, away from the party. Heal especially after AoEs and comet explosions. If comet markers continue after the wings die, group their placements when possible.
38:
the Aetherochemical Research Facility

There are many enemy groups. Tanks and healers need suitable gear and mitigation; DPS should use their AoE rotations.

## First boss
Defeat adds and dodge attacks. When it returns to the center for a broad 270-degree attack, stand behind it.

## Route to the second boss
Prioritize the spherical cultivation system, which repeatedly electrifies the arena. Adds emerge from surrounding containers while it is being destroyed; the tank should collect them. Interrupt prototype chimeras' ice roar, or move away if the interrupt is uncertain.

Its transformed forms all cleave forward: non-tanks should avoid its front. The first serpent form deals heavy damage. The second form uses a petrifying gaze, requiring players to face away, and places fire circles on random players: spread them apart.

The mechanical form immobilizes a player in a small gold circle. One other player must enter, for two total, to prevent heavy damage. A thin red marker above a player's head indicates another shared-damage attack: stack together.

## Route to the final encounters
The armored enemy on the platform cleaves and hits hard. Avoid its other attacks.

## Two-boss encounter
The tank must hold both bosses. Heal through the strong party-wide shadow flare. Fire orbs require moving away; ice orbs require standing beneath them. Tethered orbs approach one another. For tethered fire orbs, use the edge between the two untethered fire orbs. For tethered ice orbs, stand between the tethered pair.

With short ice and long fire, wait in the center for the ice, then move to the safe area away from the fire.

For Universal Manipulation, handle the effects in this order: stack, spread, stack, then break tethers by moving away from the linked player. Heal mistakes promptly. the Aery

Incoming damage can be high throughout this leveling dungeon.

## First boss: Rangda
Move close for its lightning-cloud attack. When tethered, run to a pillar to transfer the tether to it. Adds appear midway through the fight; if both DPS switch promptly, the tank may not need to collect them. Strong groups can finish the boss with the adds still present.

Defeat the dragons along the route.

Combustible Gas creates wind circles at the edge and moving white clouds inside. Wind circles inflict a painful bleeding effect. Clouds explode after a delay: find the gaps, as getting hit applies vulnerability. These mechanics can overlap other attacks, so heal players who are hit.

Some dragons telegraph frontal attacks through raised arms or a charging posture rather than a cast bar: move away from their front. In the large square before the boss, smaller dragons arrive in waves from every side. Stay together so the tank can gather them with AoE enmity.

## Final boss: Nidhogg
Remain fairly close behind the boss when possible. Avoidable AoEs apply vulnerability. Immediately leave the black eye-shaped ground marks. When a player is trapped in a dark orb, the other DPS and healer should destroy it; the tank should keep the boss steady because it cleaves.

40:
Pharos Sirius (Hard)

## Entrance to the first boss
Large pulls are possible. Prioritize large slimes before they divide into many smaller ones.

## First boss: Ghrah Luminary
Notice the untargetable birds and spiders in the dark arena. Transfer a player tether to a bird if possible, otherwise a spider. The tether later activates that creature. Kill birds; spiders also leave poison puddles and must be killed. If a player fails to transfer the tether, a humanoid add appears. Focus it immediately: it hits very hard and buffs the boss. ## Route to the second boss
Prioritize makeshift bomb incubators.

## Second boss: 8th Order Patriarch Be Gu
When it punctures the floor, a ranged DPS can tag the resulting slime, lead it onto the aether vent, and kill it there to plug the hole. A capable healer can handle this if no ranged DPS is available; otherwise assign a melee DPS. When workers and engines drop in, prioritize engines tethered to the boss, then finish the workers.

In the largest final room, three bomb boilers produce bombs that destroy walls and release more enemies. Failing to stop the boilers before walls break can overwhelm the party.

Handle attacks and adds normally in the first half. Later, blue remedy bombs move toward red bombs. Stand on the red bomb's side and hit the blue bomb with a ranged attack to push it away. Do not let them touch, or heavy party-wide damage follows.
41:
Saint Mocianne's Arboretum

## Entrance to the first boss

- Jagd Dolls buff nearby enemies' defense and have a very strong frontal cleave. Prioritize them.
- Gobwidow G-IX enemies apply vulnerability to tanks. Split a widow from other enemies; with two widows, each tank takes one.
- Gobwalker G-VII enemies also apply vulnerability, but have low HP and lower damage; modest mitigation is generally sufficient.

The driver may stay out for the first two waves but must board by the third, when the first Gobwalker appears.
- Heavy shot slows ordinary enemies but does not affect large enemies.
- Stun shot affects enemies in front, but not mechanical targets. Use it on Gordian soldiers appearing with widows in wave eight, then kill them promptly.
- Acid shot applies vulnerability, up to five stacks, useful on dolls and widows.
- Electromagnet pulls bombs: this is the essential action.
- Recharge targets a Gobwalker below 20% HP to restore energy. Normal-mode kills are often too fast for this; abandon an empty vehicle if necessary.

## Bomb handling
Pull bombs to the northeast corner, away from the party. Select them from the enemy list when convenient. Electromagnet has a fifteen-yalm range, and a distant bomb may require two pulls. There is generally only time for two uses before detonation, so watch positioning and newly appearing enemies.

Stunning soldiers and applying vulnerability are secondary tasks only when no bomb needs attention. Do not exceed five vulnerability stacks and watch your energy. Vehicles are disposable: after dismounting they eventually self-destruct, so do not exit casually.

168:
the Weeping City of Mhach

The spider adds leave a Digesting debuff when defeated; no special response is needed.

Arachne Eve
Avoid the rear tail swipe. Three red markers place webs; put them near the edge. Webs slow movement but are useful later.

After all knots die, everyone returns to the ground. If the boss survives to quicksand, stand on a web away from the center to avoid being sucked in.

Before Boss 2
Group and defeat the enemies; no special mechanics are noted.

Forgall
Green orbs create green circles. Standing in one grants Gradual Zombification; standing in overlapping circles turns you into a zombie.
Players must occupy the red circles with dark pillars. First dodge any overlapping AoEs, then return to a pillar. Each inflicts damage over time, so use one player per pillar. Unoccupied pillars make the following raidwide lethal.
Players marked with red inverted triangles gather together, normally beneath the boss. Two or three marked players can group separately if they cannot reach the others. Failing to group causes heavy damage and turns players into frogs. Long red-arrow markers instead require moving away from everyone; these receive repeated AoEs.
Add phase: party A takes the summoned Dahak at 9 o'clock, B the nightmare at 12, and C Haagenti at 3. Face Dahak sideways so its breath and tail do not point toward the center. Stun the nightmare's mist cast. Look away from Haagenti's Mortal Ray; Doom from failing to do so can be dispelled. Prefer killing nightmare and Haagenti before Dahak.
After the transition, always enter one green circle when the orbs appear, avoiding overlaps. Gradual Zombification is needed to survive Mega Death.

Before Boss 3
At the stone-face encounter, A goes left and C right to the circular platforms to kill adds; ranged players must enter before the platforms seal. Return to the center afterward. When the face casts its inscription attack, stand in the circle before it to raise the barrier. Melee may keep attacking until shortly before the cast ends, but must enter the barrier in time.

Ozma
You can fall off. Party B uses the entrance platform, A the left platform, and C the right; assign markers clockwise. Tanks stand separately from their parties, with the other players to the tank's right.
Large black meteor markers target one player per party initially and two later. Place them at your platform's back-right corner or your party's assigned marker, never overlapping. Return to the party when the black marker disappears. Kill the adds left by the meteors immediately or they cause raidwide damage.
Triangle form: leave the rectangular platform for the ring walkway to avoid the line attack, then return. Small marked AoEs inflict dispellable Bleeding. Acceleration Bomb requires stopping all actions, including auto-attacks, when its timer reaches zero. Melee and physical ranged players should turn away and cancel targeting if necessary.
Cube form: stay on your party's platform close to Ozma; the ring walkway is covered by a circular AoE. Each party's tank receives a line attack and should mitigate. Blue orbs travel clockwise around the ring and must be intercepted. One player's HP normally covers only one orb; healers can heal themselves between interceptions. Return to the platform before the knockback.
Black Hole sends everyone into another dimension. At least four players stand on each party's long platform to remove the neighboring large add's invulnerability. Kill these adds, then drop down to attack Ozma's shadow. Look away from its Assimilation cast; failing grants a stacking debuff that traps players at four stacks. Destroy the resulting blocks to free them. Once the shadow dies, jump into the center to return. Repeat the normal form mechanics.

Calofisteri
Watch which side of her hair becomes a dark blade, then move to the other side immediately; waiting for the ground marker is too late. Tanks can turn the boss to make a safe side, but should leave her still if unsure. Healers watch party HP.
After Hair Extension, avoid purple circles. Touching one creates a much larger trap that swallows a player; destroy it promptly or the player dies.
During adds, a burrowing beam marker also targets a player. Run around the edge, keeping its path away from others.
In the final phase, Hair Extension creates regular yellow AoEs. Stand directly under the double-bladed axe-shaped hair, away from round seed-shaped hair. Choosing the wrong object causes heavy damage, knockback and vulnerability.
Penetrating Shriek creates three circles in the center. Look away from the boss, preferably toward the entrance, to be knocked back. Facing her pulls you inward and adds vulnerability.
Before her charging attack, check her facing and hair. Tanks should position her in advance: the charge is immediately followed by a hair cleave, which can hit the entire alliance if aimed badly.
169:
the Final Steps of Faith

Mark A in the center and B halfway between the center and the south edge. Tank Nidhogg centrally facing north, away from the gathered party. Dodge the large eye circles placed under random players, and the clearly marked Hot Wing, Hot Tail and dive attacks.
At the add phase, the main tank takes the four-legged physical dragon at 9 o'clock; the off-tank takes the serpent-shaped magic dragon at 3. The dragon at 12 does not need tanking. Kill the main tank's add, then the off-tank's, then the remaining dragon. Avoid the untanked dragon's roaming swipe attacks. Both tanked adds have painful cones; heal the tanks. Failing to kill the adds causes a wipe.
Gather at B for healing and shields after the adds. When the raidwide ends, the main tank returns to A to pick up the boss. The tankbuster requires mitigation and healing; dodge the marked attacks.
When the boss flies away and lightning fills the arena, gather at A, locate the eyes and dive marker, and move to safety. Everyone, including the main tank, then stacks at B for Akh Morn's shared repeated hits. Afterward the main tank moves north to turn the frontal fire cleave away; everyone else stays put.
When large eyes appear on the ground, move toward the corners. Fireballs under the boss explode in crosses, making the north, east, south and west lines unsafe.
If the fight continues, repeat Akh Morn, eyes and fireballs, then Hot Wing/Hot Tail. The next fireballs may begin in a corner but still explode in crosses. Each Akh Morn sequence has an additional hit; healers should prioritize recovery, especially with new players.
170:
the Minstrel's Ballad: Nidhogg's Rage

Mark A in the center using the floor pattern; put B halfway between A and the entrance. Most Extreme attacks have no ground warning.
Start with Nidhogg central, facing away from the party. When he flies away, gather at A and find him. His dive covers half the arena. If he is centered on an edge, he dives through the middle; the outer quarter on either side is safe.
Adds: the main tank takes the four-legged dragon at 3 o'clock and the off-tank the serpent at 9. After its first lightning breath, the off-tank brings the serpent close to the other add for cleave damage, keeping their cones away from the party and each other. Once the four-legged add dies, the main tank provokes the serpent; the off-tank can Shirk or otherwise surrender aggro. Both apply vulnerability, so focus damage and heal promptly. The untanked dragon uses swipes and a breath toward the farthest player; normally a scholar, or a ranged DPS, baits this away.
After the transition, marked players place black circles at the edge. A tether then selects a random player. The off-tank intercepts it and moves away from everyone with mitigation.
Fang and Claw: three blue-tethered players attack the blue Fang. Three red-tethered players intercept the black edge orbs; leave nearby orbs to melee when possible. After interception, one blue player gets a stack marker and gathers at A with all three red players. The debuffs then reset and the mechanic repeats. The other tank is selected next: swap only after the main tank receives the blue debuff, not before.
Fang usually dies first with current damage. Claw loses HP only when its tethered players take damage; after Fang dies, attack the boss while still handling orbs and stacks. The later tower phase is often skipped; this source does not provide its full handling.
Final phase: gather at A for the dive, dodge, then gather at B for Akh Morn. The main tank turns the boss away afterward.
When the large black eyes appear beneath players, move under the boss only after they appear. Wait for the outer fireballs to explode, then move into any corner to avoid the cross blasts. Return to B for Akh Morn and swap tanks, then turn the boss away again.
Watch which upper-corner fireball appears first. If upper-left, gather bottom-right; if upper-right, gather bottom-left. Wait at the edge for the black eyes, then move toward A. Pause just outside the black circle until the central bomb explodes, continue inward, then turn left or right near A to shelter under a wing from Hot Wing.
Return to B for Akh Morn. Repeat tank swap, move under the boss, corners, and stack until defeated.
171:
Sohr Khai

Aymeric joins the party when using Duty Support. The final arena resembles the Dragonsong's Reprise victory scene but has a different floor pattern.

Before Boss 1
About three groups follow the gate. A full pull is possible but risky. Fans cast knockbacks and leave wind circles on death; entering these grants useful Haste.

Chieftain Moglin
Kill Captain Mogsun first because it makes the boss invulnerable. With high damage, the other two adds can be ignored; otherwise kill them.
The boss periodically places a revival circle. Any defeated moogle inside revives at full HP when the cast finishes. Hit the moogles with any action to push them outside.
Mogstaff creates an untargetable spinning staff. Avoid its four cardinal directions; it later fires a cross-shaped AoE.

Before Boss 2
Focus one or two eggs first. The large birds deal heavy raidwide damage; a full pull is possible but risky.

Poqhiraj
The line attack targets the tank; others should not stand with the tank, who can position near the edge.
When the boss flies and lands, it breaks part of the wall. Line up with an intact section for the following knockback.
Thundercloud marks a player and later places a cloud at their position, destroying nearby wall sections. Place it by an already broken wall or along the edge to minimize damage. Once the marker disappears and the cloud appears, everyone moves away immediately.

Before Boss 3
No special mechanics are noted.

Hraesvelgr
For the wing attack, move to the side with the unlit wing.
When the boss disappears to an edge: without ice, wait at the outer sides away from the advancing ground fire, then move to the center immediately after his central dive to avoid remaining fire. With ice, slide to the sides after the dive marker appears, then dodge the red circles.

172:
Hullbreaker Isle (Hard)

The tentacle minion is one possible reason to revisit this dungeon.

Before Boss 1
Prioritize the bulls and coeurls that create buff circles. Tanks pull enemies out of those circles.

Sanguine Sirens
This encounter consists of several enemies. Tanks should pick up anything attacking the healer. Kill the coeurls first and dodge the marked attacks.

Before Boss 2
Enemies hit hard but have no special mechanics noted here.

Ymir
Players marked for the lightning attack stand in a puddle. Break tethers by moving apart, and dodge other marked attacks. The boss freezes the floor, causing sliding that can inconvenience melee players.

Before Boss 3
No special mechanics are noted.

Eynzahr Slafyrsyn
At a health threshold he changes form. He poisons players and places antidotes and bombs in the surrounding chests. Watch the slow animation to identify an antidote chest, then move to it after the chest closes to cure the poison. Leaving it untreated gives Damage Down.

182:
Xelphatol

Expect many enemies; use area damage. Several casts can be interrupted, so tanks should have Interject available.

Marked circular AoEs damage both players and enemies and apply vulnerability. They can be baited onto adds, but avoid being hit yourself.

Nuzal Hueloc
When the boss flies up, adds and balloon turrets appear. Destroy a balloon turret. When the dark ground marker appears, stand underneath the boss in the indicated area. The balloon explosion's updraft brings him down. Kill adds and dodge marked attacks.
The boss applies dispellable Bleeding to random players; healers cleanse it and restore HP.

Before Boss 2
The gorillas use 120-degree cones that Interject can interrupt. Later two appear together, so be ready to dodge. Stay reasonably close and avoid the damaging spikes around the wooden platform. The caged piglets resemble the final boss's minion drop.

Dotoli Ciloc
Avoid the edge spikes. For the strong wind knockback, align with a barricade using the floor pattern as a guide. From the second use onward, wind circles block two barricades; choose another.
The attack after the boss makes itself light deals heavy damage. Healers should prepare and tanks mitigate if it is not avoided; this source does not give a reliable dodge method.

Before Boss 3
The mist casters attack from range, so gather other enemies onto them.

Tozol Huatotl
Dodge the marked attacks and respond to spread and stack markers. Garuda's summoned attacks overlap other mechanics, making the arena crowded. Stay calm and use the edges while leaving room for teammates.
183:
Containment Bay P1T6

Most attacks are clearly marked. Watch both sides when Sophia disappears for a line dive. Her floating head can also disappear independently and fire a line attack from an edge.

184:
Containment Bay P1T6 (Extreme)

Mark A at top-right. The main tank must distinguish the spell names. Dodge Thunder II by moving beside or through Sophia, then return.
Four clones appear. If the first tether selects one clone, the main tank dodges Thunder II through the boss, then everyone hides behind that clone, accounting for its facing, or in a gap without a clone. If the first tethers select two clones, first stand under Sophia for the initial lightning attack, then under either of those original two clones for the later attacks.

The First shields either front/back or sides; if you missed which, stop attacking until the shield expires. Its charge-marked player stands close, while others avoid the charge path.
