186:
Alexander - The Eyes of the Creator

The gatekeeper's frontal auto-attacks can be shared. Both tanks can face it together with mitigation.
Divide the arena into four quarters around the boss. Mark A in the southeast. Keep the boss's initial facing; everyone else attacks from behind and avoids its frontal cleave.
Glowing floor sections later fill with lava. A player, usually a healer, picks up power generators and places them on fallen adds to revive them. The first person to attack a revived add gets aggro. Kill revived adds on the glowing section so the lava consumes their remains. Otherwise the boss absorbs them, regenerates its arms and makes later mechanics stronger or impossible.
First wave: bodies land northeast and northwest, while lava will appear northeast. Leave the northeast bodies alone; revive and move the northwest ones.
Second wave: bodies land northwest, lava southwest. The main tank leaves room. These adds can be grouped close to the boss for area damage.
During or after each wave, red markers place scrap piles. Put them close to the boss, then hide behind them during Scrapburst.
After the second wave comes a 270-degree attack. The main tank uses heavy mitigation; everyone else shelters behind the boss. Regenerated arms may require an invulnerability or dodging, and fully completed arms turn it into an unavoidable full-circle wipe.
Afterward, a proximity marker northwest drops an armored Faust. The off-tank takes it to A southeast, facing outward. Kill Faust first. Floor sections light in order northwest, southwest, southeast, northeast; kill it before lava reaches its position, or it causes raidwide damage. Avoid both Faust's frontal attacks and the main boss's cleave.
Repeat reviving, moving and killing adds for lava disposal.
187:
Alexander - The Breath of the Creator

The initial trash has no special mechanics noted. Pull the boss into an empty upper-left or upper-right area. Never step on the three central buttons; reducing battle effects may help you see them.
The rear crystal button triggers line attacks down the sides. The middle hammer button drops hammers over all three buttons. The entrance nail button raises floor spikes and roots players.
A red marker with a tether means move away from the boss. Everyone else avoids the tether's line, which is lethal.
When the boss jumps onto the crystal button, move toward the middle. When it jumps onto the hammer button, move to the outer edge.
The boss later becomes invulnerable at one side while Gobroller VI appears opposite. Its Steam Roller cast ends with a forward slam. Tanks and melee must leave before the cast finishes or be crushed.
After the roller dies, the main tank heavily mitigates the boss's charge and healers restore HP.
After Single Charge, the boss shows a red or green overhead marker: red means move away, green means move close.
Frequent raidwides and smaller tankbusters follow. Healers watch everyone. Stand between the saws when they appear along the sides.
If the fight lasts longer, the button-jump sequence repeats.
188:
Alexander - The Heart of the Creator

Dodge the early marked attacks. The second Optical Sight covers a large central area; move outward in advance. Switch promptly to adds.
For the charged cannon, the off-tank receives an expanding white-triangle marker. Take it to the edge with heavy mitigation; everyone else stays as far away as possible.
When the boss returns to the middle, click one of the boarding interaction points around the arena to jump onto it. After it bombs the platform, complete the active-time maneuver by pressing keys to jump back down; failing causes a fatal fall.
Four crystals may then appear unless skipped by high damage. Destroy them. The following dark raidwide also applies damage over time; heal through it.
After Limit Cut, the boss reappears in the center with a plasma shield. Everyone must attack from the front to damage the shield.
After it breaks, the boss marks the main tank for a charge. The tank uses strong mitigation and moves away from the party; the charge kills other players along its path. Since the party was attacking the front shield, moving through the boss to the opposite side is generally safer.
For the strong propeller wind, hide behind a large fallen object or become Confused.
The final adds knock their tank back in a line. The off-tank collects them centrally and faces them away from the party, then the party kills them.
189:
Alexander - The Soul of the Creator

Keep the boss central. It has an unmarked frontal cone; everyone else avoids the main tank's side.
For Sacrament, move backward between the two untethered points. Tethered directions fire lethal rectangular lasers. Red-marked DPS move away from others; healers prepare for heavy damage.
During adds, tanks collect enemies promptly. The third wave includes four fixed-position enemies around the edge that repeatedly cast raidwide attacks. Kill those four one at a time before the remaining adds.
After adds, the boss appears north for Divine Judgment. When the warning says five seconds remain, use tank Limit Break 3. Other mitigation is optional; omitting the tank LB is fatal.
During Time Stop, green-marked players move away, while everyone else stacks behind the boss. After resolution, the boss appears at the edge and casts Sacrament; move toward its sides, avoiding all tethered laser directions.
After two Time Stops, the boss returns centrally and four black orbs appear. DPS enter the orbs and kill the enemies inside. A healer or off-tank can substitute if necessary, but the main tank must stay outside. Outside, red markers still require separation and heavy healing, and Sacrament continues.
When the inside players return, dodge the black circles of Gravitational Anomaly through the gaps. Later Time Stops combine stack/spread, Gravitational Anomaly and Sacrament. Black circles become safe once they turn white.
Finally a huge Alexander tethers four players. They move apart to place four successive circles, then resume Time Stop handling.

the Great Gubal Library (Hard)

Demon of the Tome

219:
Baelsar's Wall

Enemies arrive from several directions on one platform. Tanks pick them up promptly.

Armored Weapon

220:
Dun Scaith

Deathgaze Hollow
The ship's bow and stern are safe boundaries. You can fall off the side edges.
Void Death creates a red-black central circle and pulls twice. Run outward immediately; the second pull resolves instantly, so a slow start can be fatal.
Void Aero creates a central tornado. Stand beside it, not inside, and position so the knockback sends you toward the bow or stern rather than over a side.
For Void Blizzard followed by wind, move opposite the proximity marker. After the large ice block lands, shelter behind it against the following wind.

Ferdiad Hollow
Wormhole: edge Atomos link to either an orb or a ring. An orb represents a point-blank AoE; a ring represents a donut with a safe center. If neither is a ring, stay away from the untethered Atomos. If both are rings, either untethered Atomos is safe underneath.
Debilitator gives everyone either fire or water resistance down. Step on the floor switches until all show the opposite element: fire vulnerability requires water; water vulnerability requires fire. Scathach

Diabolos

221:
Sohm Al (Hard)

Trash can be more dangerous than the bosses.

Before Boss 1
Ground vents can apply vulnerability to nearby enemies. Pull enemies onto them to help clear a large pull.

Leightonward
Avoid the spore pods. Large pods cause proximity-based raidwide damage, so move farther away.

Before Boss 2
Expect many enemies.

Gowrow
Watch the animations. A raised arm attacks the tank. A raised tail can mean a tail swipe or a circular attack; do not linger behind it. Lowering one shoulder signals a charge. Folding its arms signals a fireball or breath; avoid the front.

Before Boss 3
Immediately focus the gel-like Blood of the Mountain enemies. If two appear, mark and kill them in order. Stun their casts; if one explodes, heal the party urgently.

Lava Scorpion
Its jumping crush creates a large lava patch. Marked players place it near the edge. Prioritize red adds when it calls them. The second call summons four adds; a ranged DPS can prepare a Limit Break to clear them.
223:
Containment Bay Z1T9

Face Zurvan away from the party. The circular platform breaks apart section by section; do not fall. Dodge the marked attacks until the final platform gives way and everyone lands below.
His frontal cleave reaches very far, so the main tank keeps him facing away throughout. A north marker can help maintain orientation. Southern Cross places ice circles beneath players at cast completion; watch the cast and move promptly.
Dodge circles and lines, and gather for stack markers, usually centrally. When Wave Cannon selects a player, avoid the boss's front.
Adds: DPS first kill the stationary casting Wile add while the two tanks collect the others. Then kill the Will add, followed by the remaining enemies.
After three waves and Ahura Mazda, the last phase adds fire and ice brands. Enter an ice tower with the ice brand and a fire tower with the fire brand. Other attacks work as before and have ground warnings.
224:
Containment Bay Z1T9 (Extreme)

Guide under construction. The source also references an external illustrated guide.
235:
Shisui of the Violet Tides

Before Boss 1
Anglerfish hide in the sand and damage anyone stepping on them. Avoid triggering them unnecessarily, especially with an unfamiliar healer.

Amikiri
When it targets a player, destroy its leg to flip it over and make it vulnerable. Kill adds first. Players with blue-orb markers spread apart; sufficient damage can kill the target before those markers resolve.

Before Boss 2
Do not run ahead of the tank. Choose single or double pulls to suit the party's gear.

Ruby Princess
During Seduce, open one of the four corner chests to become old and avoid attraction. If someone uses your chest, standing against the wall behind it, in line with the boss, can let the forced movement carry you through the chest effect at the right time.
After the undersea volcano attack, a targeted player must keep running away from others to dodge repeated heavy hits. Taking three or more consecutively is fatal.

Before Boss 3
Pufferfish explode on contact. Pull enemies into the little treasure-chest alcove to avoid them.

Shisui Yohi
When she submerges, three bubbles apply three damage-over-time stacks. Destroying each removes one stack. An undergeared healer should prioritize keeping the party alive. After the bubbles die, watch the water ripples and avoid where the boss resurfaces; the attack covers roughly half the arena.
236:
the Temple of the Fist

This is a monk training ground. The second boss is graded by kill time.

Before Boss 1
Stay away from the green moss-like objects. Approaching makes them burst and leave sticky ground.

Coeurl Smriti and Coeurl Sruti
Only one begins the fight. Pick up the second promptly when it joins. Watch the red coeurl's cone attacks in particular.

Before Boss 2
Tanks should not fight enemies on top of floor mechanisms, making melee movement easier.

Arbuda
For front-and-back slices, move to a side. For side slices, move in front or behind. After its anticipation cast, watch the animation: shields protect three sides, leaving only one safe direction to attack from, including for casters. Sun/moon markers require the matching glowing floor.
The observing NPC rates your kill time, from slowest to fastest: moss spirit, chapuli, gazelle, coeurl, griffin, the two-headed coeurl record matching Ivon, then a new temple record at destroyer level.

Before Boss 3
No special mechanics are noted. Well-equipped parties can clear the route in two pulls.

Ivon Coeurlfist
A heavy hit targets the farthest player; ranged DPS can bait it. Healers prepare recovery. When the boss tethers to chakra orbs, everyone intercepts the orbs. Clearing all of them reduces the following AoE damage.
238:
the Sirensong Sea

This is the first dungeon after level 60. Some enemies shown as skeletons in the global client appear as zombies in the Chinese version.

Before Boss 1
Pull the enemies to Lyse on the starboard side so she can help with area attacks. The lobsters' tail attack is less severe than the similarly named level-50 attack.

Lugat
Dodge the marked attacks and share stack markers.

Before Boss 2
On the intervening ships, their bow decks offer safety from AoEs. The final ship has no such safe spot, so dodge the ground markers.

The Governor
Dodge through the available gaps calmly. When a DPS is caught, move away from the boss immediately to break the shadow connection.

Before Boss 3
Stun the gatekeeper's seductive howl to prevent the following heavy damage.

Lorelei
Her casts force players to move forward or backward. Check the required direction and adjust your facing so the forced movement does not take you into a blue circle.
239:
the Royal Menagerie

Shinryu's hitbox reaches the arena center, so melee can attack there. Merely targeting him does not pull, but right-clicking can start auto-attacks. Players generally fight centrally and move into his hitbox to dodge.
His first attack is Tidal Wave. Find the water pillar when you hear water or see the cast, then stand against that edge. Knockback prevention can instead be used about halfway through the cast.
Share Supernova in water. Stand in water for Hellfire too. Lightning-arrow markers spread apart outside water, and everyone avoids water for Judgment Bolt. Red-arrow targets move to the sides, preferably together without covering the whole arena; others have more room near the boss.
Akh Morn is shared by the two tanks with mitigation; other players stay clear.
During adds, the large dragons have painful frontal cleaves and the small ones use AoEs. Melee can focus large dragons to avoid the smaller ground attacks.
After adds, complete the active-time maneuver by pressing ordinary keys; avoid modifier, Windows and Enter keys.
The new arena is a three-by-three grid. The opening dive is extremely wide, leaving two corners safe; Sprint can help. Break tethers by separating. Whenever the tail lands, switch to it immediately: destroying it deals huge damage to Shinryu.
White repeated markers, distinct from the tanks' Akh Morn, pursue a random player; move away from their previous positions.
He also uses earlier primals' signature attacks. For Earthen Fury, gather on the middle tile because another tile breaks. Diamond Dust freezes the floor; avoid movement inputs while it is slippery. For Aerial Blast, move continually toward the central tornado so the wind does not push you off.
240:
Bardam's Mettle

The open scenery can make it tempting to wander off. One boss is a noncombat trial.

Before Boss 1
A full pull is possible but risky: bears and bulls hit hard and apply painful Bleeding. Consider gear and experience before combining groups.

Garula
Dodge the quickly executed, varied large AoEs. Its charge deals proximity damage. A target remaining within eight yalms is unlikely to survive, so move far away.

Before Boss 2
Large enemies hit hard; healers stay alert.

Bardam
You cannot attack or use actions. Dodge the mechanics and occupy towers through three trials. Two failures in a trial immobilize you. The party only needs one player to pass.

Before Boss 3
At the mud creature with two butterflies, stay toward the left: a large iron ball rolls down from farther along the route.

Yol
Dodge AoEs and look away from gaze attacks. There is substantial damage for healers. During adds, the boss dives from the side where an add appears. Tanks can move the add out of the dive path early; others dodge.
After the boss's second flight and landing, gather centrally beneath it and focus the wings. A caster Limit Break is useful; physical ranged aiming is less convenient and a melee LB is unnecessary here.
241:
Doma Castle

Enemies deal heavy damage.

Before Boss 1
A full pull is possible but strongly discouraged.

Magitek Rearguard
Dodge the many different ground attacks. Casters, especially black mages, should be careful about committing to long casts.

Before Boss 2
Follow the tank through the three lines of magitek artillery. Avoid a full pull unless the group is coordinated.

Magitek Hexadrone
Share stacks and occupy towers while managing the electric fences. You can move when the fences first appear. The tank should position the boss in the largest clear area for possible stacks. Enter towers promptly; once the fence's red detection area activates, leaving a tower unoccupied is preferable to being repeatedly knocked around. Healers prepare emergency healing for missed towers or undersized stacks.

Before Boss 3
The final magitek spider has high HP, hits hard and gains reinforcements. Do not relax too early.

Grynewaht
After Chainsaw starts casting, the tank can sidestep out of the original position. If marked as an incoming impact center, move into an empty corner until the position locks, about four seconds, then return. The gunfire line selects one player and cannot be avoided by that target; aim it away from everyone else.
242:
Castrum Abania

Before Boss 1
No special mechanics are noted beyond choosing pulls sensibly.

Magna Roader
When it begins charging, kill the soldier beside a cannon and fire while the boss plans its route. One shot is enough.

Before Boss 2
Groups usually destroy the leftmost incubation tank first. With sufficient damage, two can be destroyed before opening.

Number XXIV
Three large towers appear; put at least one player in each. Barrier Shift then announces two charged elements. Enter the floor circle for the third, unmentioned element: if thunder and fire are announced, choose ice. The boss's buff also identifies which element is not reflected. Wrong-element attacks reflect damage back; only a few can kill you.

Before Boss 3
Handle the reinforcements with area damage.

Inferno
Dodge attacks and kill adds. The boss is enhanced during the fight, increasing its damage and making attacks harder to avoid. Tanks should save mitigation for enhanced tankbusters. After two enhancements, healers allow more safety margin and promptly dispel Bleeding.
243:
the Pool of Tribute

Keep Susano central. An unmarked heavy tank attack occurs shortly after the pull: the main tank mitigates after one or two global cooldowns. Healers keep tank HP high, preferably above 80%. Once aggro is secure, the off-tank can use tank stance to pick up quickly if the main tank dies.
Stay reasonably close. A random player is knocked back and then receives a stack marker. That player can position beside or in front of the boss for a shorter return, then immediately rejoin everyone to share. Avoid lining up yourself, Susano and an edge thundercloud; reposition before the knockback to avoid the cloud's line attack.
Sword phase: the main tank interacts with the glowing sword-catching point near the center and completes the key-press maneuver. A suitably level-synced player can substitute if needed. The off-tank intercepts orbs around the edge, clockwise through roughly 2, 4 and 9 o'clock. Everyone else attacks the blade behind the catcher. Do this twice.
Then leave the middle as the island splits and resume the earlier mechanics. When a player is trapped in stone, attack the correct gaol: normally the one immediately above the boss in the enemy list, or the last entry if the boss is first. Free the player before its cast finishes or they die.
244:
the Pool of Tribute (Extreme)

Phase 1
An unmarked tank hit comes shortly after the pull. Mitigate after two or three actions; healers recover the tank. It repeats two or three times with time to heal between.
Four players receive countdown markers. Stop all actions, movement and auto-attacks when the timer reaches zero, then resume once it resolves. Cancel targeting or sheath if necessary.
A red marker means knockback followed by a stack. Position so you can return quickly. If thunderclouds line up in front and behind, take the knockback sideways to avoid their line attacks.

Phase 2
A tank catches the sword at the glowing central interaction point. The other tank uses mitigation and intercepts orbs clockwise, normally starting around 1 o'clock. DPS attack the blade and healers continue healing.
Swap duties for the second catch because the first catcher has slashing resistance down. After both, everyone moves west to avoid the large attack.

Phase 3
The dark middle strip applies Sinking and kills anyone remaining over five seconds.
Stormsplitter is a tankbuster with severe slashing vulnerability. The off-tank provokes during its cast.
Ordinary purple markers require the target to cross to the opposite half, then return when the marker disappears. Four players are marked in succession each cycle. From the third cycle, a purple marker may have a tall vertical tether: that target stays still while everyone else crosses instead.
Repeated raidwides require sustained healing.
Free the stone-gaol target by attacking the appropriate Ame-no-Iwato in the enemy list: immediately above the boss if present there, otherwise the last entry.
247:
Ala Mhigo

Complete your level-70 job quest first to obtain the job equipment and final action.

Before Boss 1
There are many enemies. New or inexperienced groups should use smaller pulls; two groups of pulls normally suffice, but reduce further if needed.

Guard Scorpion
Dodge the attacks. Tracking circles move slowly but strike quickly once their positions lock. Keep moving if unsure, or leave immediately after the position is fixed.

Before Boss 2
Use at least two pulls rather than taking everything together.

Aulus mal Asina
When separated from your body, return to it. Lasers stun you and floating claws push you away. If time is short, intentionally angle a claw's push toward your body. Healers watch inexperienced players during the frequent ground attacks.

Before Boss 3
Clear the route steadily.

Zenos
Tethered players move close to the boss and face the resulting cone toward the edge or empty space. For the wind attack, stand close to the wind orb for its knockback. For lightning, leave the visible effect area. For the sword line attacks, all four players spread and aim lines apart; four overlapping hits are fatal. If a tether and wind overlap, position between the wind orb and the tethered NPC, close to the orb.
When three swords appear, focus them with full damage: faster kills reduce the following AoE. Continue handling all three attack types while killing swords.
252:
Deltascape V1.0

An unmarked frontal tail cleave hits the main tank throughout. Use some mitigation early, heal the tank and keep everyone else away from the front.
Fireballs grow before exploding. First, four appear centrally; move away during the roar. Next they appear around the edges and the boss moves to an edge for Downburst, pushing the balls. Stand close to the boss at that edge.
Twin Bolt hits the main tank and their nearest player. The off-tank should stand closest and share with mitigation.
For ice, lightning circles and a stack: spread before the floor fully freezes, place lightning circles apart, then slide back behind the boss. There is a short period after thawing to adjust for the stack.
First Classical Elements: central fireballs are pushed outward; gather centrally to avoid them. Once surrounding balls explode, move outward to place lightning circles.
The next balls begin inside, then outside with a push. Move close to the boss as soon as it appears at the edge.
Charybdis reduces everyone to one HP. Heal immediately before the following raidwide.
Second Classical Elements: outer balls appear, then four inner ones. Stand between adjacent inner balls. The push, outer explosions and freezing occur together; correct your position if necessary. The displaced inner balls then explode, followed by a stack behind the boss.
Later attacks repeat these combinations; handle each calmly.
253:
Deltascape V2.0

Use the duty action, Anti-gravity Gimbal, before the pull to gain Levitation. It is used frequently. Avoid the main tank's unmarked frontal cleave. Levitation avoids Earthquake and can also resolve sinking into the floor. The tankbuster requires mitigation and healing.
Gravitational Manipulation fixes a player's height high or low and gives a stack marker. Match that height to share: use the duty action for a high stack.
Tentacles appear at four red edge markers with blue eyes above them. Some eyes disappear; stay away from tentacles whose eyes remain. Their attacks are very large. On the final pattern, only one tentacle is safe; stand outside it toward the edge.
Dark orbs come at ground level in black or at levitating height in yellow, alongside a look-away mechanic.
Four black orbs: levitate and look away from the boss.
Four black and four yellow: stay grounded centrally between black orbs, and look away. Levitation would put you into yellow orbs.
Three black and three yellow in a line: use an orb-free area. A knock-up and AoE follow; heal promptly on landing.
Four yellow orbs: stay grounded until their attack visibly resolves, then immediately use the duty action for the accompanying sinking or Earthquake.
254:
Deltascape V3.0

The opening Ribbit cast turns players in a 150-degree frontal cone into frogs. Move to the side or behind.
After introductory attacks, Game Board changes the tiles. First, stand on your role's icon; both DPS tiles need a DPS.
On the blue board, a diagonal of tiles differs from the rest. Stay on that diagonal for The Queen's Waltz. An add then appears northeast: the off-tank faces its cone away and DPS kill it first while dodging the boss.
Mindjack forces movement in the named direction. Set your facing to travel safely and move onto a safe tile immediately afterward.
The boss later sends everyone into a sand maze. Sand tiles force travel along their arrows. Your first step should be away from the exit: if the exit is directly left, step right. Finishing quickly awards Damage Up and Haste; taking too long kills you, though you can be raised.
After the maze, familiar mechanics overlap. For Holy with forced movement, gather beforehand so everyone moves together while sharing. For blue lines with ice, the main tank must not bring the boss too far inward, or ice covers the safe tile. If Game Board shows frog tiles, deliberately stand in front for Ribbit to become a frog.
255:
Deltascape V4.0

Healers dispel the opening Doom from two players with Esuna.
The boss uses three elemental attacks. Blizzard is an AoE to dodge. Thunder is an area tankbuster: mitigate, keep others away, and consider swapping after more than two thunder-vulnerability stacks. Fire marks random players with circles; spread.
When the boss tethers to a black hole, those elements are enhanced. Enhanced Blizzard requires continuous movement to avoid freezing. Enhanced Thunder is a point-blank AoE: move away. Enhanced Fire is a raidwide with Pyretic: stop actions until the debuff ends, and heal afterward. Check for the tether during the cast to distinguish enhanced from ordinary versions.
Vacuum Wave knocks back when its cast ends; knockback prevention works. Holy is a shared stack.
For The Decisive Battle, move outward from the central proximity attack, then dodge the emerging head by going behind or to its side. The barriers break, so you can now fall.
Flare marks three players with white triangles; each moves away from the others and the party. Mitigate Meteor. Do not touch the black-hole orbs. Continue responding to the three elements as before.
262:
Kugane Castle

The Japanese-style courtyards are popular for screenshots.

Zuiko-maru
Players tethered to adds move toward the edge, or gather the tethered add with another add to kill them together. This makes their self-destruct attacks easier to avoid.

Before Boss 2
Kill summoning ninjas immediately. The final room has three; a ranged Limit Break can help kill them before the summons finish. Otherwise large-headed enemies appear with painful attacks. If they spawn, tanks mitigate and healers give extra healing, especially with two together.

Dojun-maru
Dodge the attacks. If the ground gets crowded, stop attacking and concentrate on movement.

Before Boss 3
Kill the self-destructing enemies where they stand.

Yojimbo
During the fight his employer scatters coins. Collect them before Daigoro does. Clearing all coins avoids the following AoE; more remaining coins mean more damage. Their dialogue repeatedly bargains over the fee: Yojimbo demands payment, calls Daigoro to gather it, and announces progressively stronger sword strikes, including Zanmato, according to the amount offered.
When butterflies fall, first dodge outward, then move inward. The dragon heads can technically be ignored, but killing them makes collecting coins easier. Yojimbo also appears in the Hildibrand quests.
263:
Emanation

Vril negates the boss's attacks and heals you when she is not under Divine Doubt. It has limited charges; collect white orbs to restore them rather than wasting it.
The main tank uses Vril or mitigation for the tankbuster. A blue orb marks the off-tank, the player second in enmity. Move to the main tank's side to avoid cleaving the party.
Dodge other attacks. Healer-targeted circles expand; place them far back at the edge, away from everyone.
When Lakshmi becomes untargetable in the north for the transition, everyone must use Vril or die.
Divine Doubt surrounds her with dark energy. In this normal version, Vril no longer negates her damage, so tanks must mitigate. For Alluring Arm, have Vril active and move close to prevent being knocked off.
DPS cross markers must leave genuinely safe spaces, because a stack can immediately follow and taking both is lethal. A marked melee should stop repositioning once placed; use True North rather than moving the cross onto teammates. Share stacks and dodge as appropriate.
264:
Emanation (Extreme)

Keep the Vril duty action easy to reach. The off-tank must stay second in enmity. A common plan holds the boss north, puts tanks north, DPS on each side and healers south; the main tank takes the two eastern adds and off-tank the two western adds.

Phase 1
The initial two adds use circular gaze attacks. Look away or leave their circles. The fight proper begins when Lakshmi becomes targetable.
A main-tank tankbuster is immediately followed by a very wide cone on the off-tank, marked with a blue orb. The off-tank commonly handles it on the boss's right; others avoid that side.
Healer circles go to the back-left and back-right because they expand.
After Divine Doubt, her attacks strengthen and Vril is required to resist them. Both tanks use it for their tankbuster/cone; DPS and healers use it for cross and circle markers. Everyone activates Vril for the knockback or pull, moving close for the knockback and away for the pull.

Phase 2
Do not kill adds indiscriminately. Lower their HP and watch for the blue shield effect, also shown in their buffs. It periodically transfers. Kill an add while it holds the shield to gain a Vril charge. Adds revive at full HP. Collect enough charges before time expires or the transition is fatal. Healers keep healing through their attacks.
Use Vril before the transition animation.

Phase 3
For the early confusion mechanic, heal everyone to full, mitigate and use Vril to shorten the loss of control. Both tanks again use Vril for their separate attacks.
Blue orbs on light strips replenish Vril, but leave each strip immediately after collecting: it later becomes an AoE. Familiar mechanics repeat; use Vril to resist empowered attacks.
278:
the Minstrel's Ballad: Shinryu's Domain

Several mechanics can kill regardless of gear. Shinryu has a very large hitbox. Do not break the starting arena's central tile carelessly; it affects later tail placement. Watch all cast bars.
A common assignment has tanks north, DPS on the sides, healers south. Tether/stack pairs are MT with D1, ST with D2, H1 with D3 and H2 with D4. Tail placements are healer bottom-right, DPS bottom-left, then tank top-left or center. Akh Morn can be shared, then handled with main-tank invulnerability, off-tank invulnerability, then shared again. Assign one healer to slide for Diamond Dust; earth breaths go healer-left and DPS-right. Main tank takes the central large add, off-tank the others.

Phase 1
Always prioritize Shinryu's heart when it appears.
For Tidal Wave, use knockback prevention or stand at the edge on the water-pillar side. The first healer tail marker goes bottom-right.
Icicles come from the rear and each is half a tile wide; look behind you. Stand in water for Supernova and Hellfire. Leave water for lightning and Judgment Bolt, spreading for lightning. Icicles may overlap these attacks.
Both tanks share Akh Morn with heavy mitigation. Other players avoid the repeated light pillars targeted at them, and healers maintain HP.
The second tail marker targets a DPS: place bottom-left, or centrally only if that tile is not cracked.
Break other tethers by separating. Aim earth-breath markers toward the sides. For Diamond Dust, gather centrally for healing; healers then become tethered. Normally the shield healer slides diagonally forward to break the tether and slides back, while the other healer stays and heals.
Heal spirit dragons at the edge to remove their tethers. Vercure, Clemency and healing-over-time effects also work. Time is short.

Phase 2
Complete the active-time maneuver when lifted into the air. On landing, find the adjacent platform and stand at your platform's edge for the boss to knock you across.
Kill the adds and heal; the large dragon's tankbuster needs mitigation. After the raidwide, stand near the edge of the central blue circle. Once the tail lands, climb it to return to the neighboring arena.

Phase 3
Mark A in front of the boss as a positioning reference. Mitigate the opening tankbuster and provoke-swap during its cast. Break fire chains toward your paired stack positions, then share damage there.
Snowstorm plus lightning: keep moving to avoid freezing, then spread for lightning. Snowstorm plus Supernova: stand still at A to freeze deliberately; Supernova thaws you.
Afterward, dodge the huge breath cone by moving to the sides, or move forward into the dark circle beneath the boss for the roar. Leave that dark circle immediately after the roar resolves or gain Doom. Heal spirit dragons if they appear again.
Finally the boss and both wings cast together. Use the blue interaction points on either side to jump onto his back. DPS use Limit Break to help destroy both wings, then jump down and finish the body.
279:
the Drowned City of Skalla

An old rumor claims a miqo'te eating food reveals a fat cat inside the second boss; treat it as a rumor.

Before Boss 1
Walls break only after enemies die and then reveal more enemies, limiting large pulls.

Kelpie
Avoid the red edge water: it applies damage over time and vulnerability; more than three stacks strain healing. Mitigate Torpedo, the tankbuster. Rising water is a raidwide; healers especially watch players with vulnerability.
For the pull, move away; for the push, move close. A red-circle target places it at the edge and moves away immediately. The resulting tethered water orb follows its player and deals continuous damage on contact. Later pull/push overlaps markers and orbs, so healers prepare.

Before Boss 2
No special mechanics are noted.

The Old One
Dodge cones and circles under players; ranged players may find it easier to remain fairly close. The boss becomes invulnerable and links copies. Kill the first set normally. From the second set, you become a spriggan with a bomb-placement action. Place bombs slightly ahead of moving copies; they explode after about three seconds and have a generous area. Destroy every copy.

Before Boss 3
After clearing a platform, enter its magic circle to transform and float across the gaps. Watch the transformation timer or you can fall to your death.

Hrodric Poisontongue
Raised arms mean avoid the front; a raised tail means avoid the rear. Both animation and messages warn you, and failure gives vulnerability. For proximity damage, non-tanks move to the edge; a mitigating tank can remain if the healer knows. Folded arms signal an unmarked line breath, so leave the front. Handle later donuts, circles and crosses without crowding teammates' safe spots.
280:
the Unending Coil of Bahamut (Ultimate)

The source lists several external illustrated and written guides rather than an in-plugin walkthrough.
281:
the Royal City of Rabanastre

Mateus
When icy rings appear, destroy ice blocks, intercept small water orbs and occupy each fountain with at least three players. Unoccupied fountains become ice blocks tethering players; destroy these promptly to prevent freezing. After intercepting water, avoid the skating enemies or they freeze you.
Frogs appear while Breathless stacks rise. At nine stacks you suffocate. Kill frogs to produce bubbles and enter bubbles periodically to reset stacks. Aim directional AoEs away from bubbles. If three large adds appear, tanks separate them; keeping them close gives tethers and repeated raidwide damage.

Before Boss 2
Group the trash. Run as far as possible from the red chocobo's powerful proximity meteor.

Hashmal
Place party markers south for A, northwest for B and northeast for C. Prioritize survival.
The main tank's frontal cone hits hard; mitigate and keep others out. Avoid black circles where stone towers rise, then watch their cut surfaces to identify their falling direction.
When the boss jumps to an edge, one arm burns. That half is dangerous, as is the boss itself; use the opposite outer portion of the arena.
When the large central tower appears, move toward your party marker and focus sand spheres. If stone golems appear, focus them; a ranged Limit Break helps.

Before Boss 3
Prioritize chimeras. Their casts cannot be interrupted here: ice means move away, lightning means move close.

Rofocale
Assign A north, B southeast and C southwest. Prioritize movement during the later crowded AoEs.
The tankbuster gives three physical-vulnerability stacks before a heavy hit; mitigate. The targeted charge is safer for its target close to the boss, because a dangerous half-arena attack follows and a distant target may strand others. For the figure-eight charge, stand outward beside the boss; its track appears only late in the cast.
During adds, enter your party's barrier circle and kill its add. The boss circles outside and can knock players away. Tanks face adds outward.
After adds, watch the boss spiral upward. When he prepares to charge, run left or right to the edge. Alternatively, central heavy mitigation can survive, but without mitigation it is fatal.
Later blue traps expand into large claws when stepped on, binding nearby players. Others must destroy the claws or their victims die. Do not step on traps while dodging.
When the arena darkens and dark magic circles appear, right-click to close them; merely standing on them does nothing.

Argath Thadalfus
Mistakes add panic stacks; three trigger uncontrolled running with vulnerability, often fatal.
Divine Revelation shows an angel or demon face, masks around the boss and movement/gaze debuffs. The angel means obey the debuff; the demon means do the opposite. A useful rule is: angel, look away and move; demon, face the boss and stop acting.
Group tethered adds for area damage.
The rotating-finger mechanic forces movement along the finger regardless of which direction key you press. Watch the finger and time inputs; quick repeated taps allow fine adjustment. Dodge other marked attacks.
284:
Hells' Lid

This scenic dungeon begins the Four Lords quest series.

Before Boss 1
In the area surrounded by four fire walls, tanks run around to secure all enemies.

Otake-maru
Move away for 100-tonze Swing. The boss throws its weapon down and pursues a marked player with lava breath. That player runs around the arena, avoiding the lava. Everyone also stays away from the discarded weapon; the boss retrieves it afterward.

Before Boss 2
No special mechanics are noted.

Kamaitachi
Even ranged players should stay fairly close to react to half-arena attacks. When it flies, kill adds while dodging winds and lines. The boss charges along its tethers in sequence.

Before Boss 3
No special mechanics are noted.

Genbu
Dodge attacks and spread circles. The hexagonal floor displays arrows and one tile holds a water orb. Follow the arrows to predict its path and stay out of it. Later this overlaps spread markers or other AoEs. Healers can focus on healing if overwhelmed; continue handling visible attacks.
285:
the Fractal Continuum (Hard)

The story concludes part of the Ixal tribe's history.

Before Boss 1
Move away from minotaur spins. For chimeras, ice means move away and lightning means move close; the ice cast can be interrupted.

Motherbit
Dodge marked attacks. When bits line up, move behind their barrels; this attack has no ground warning.

Before Boss 2
No special mechanics are noted.

Ultima Warrior
Avoid the frontal charged line, signaled by its cast and an obvious green sphere. It uses the Warring Triad's powers: pair one black and one white marker for Sophia's attack; match your fire/ice brand to the same-colored circle for Zurvan's; place marked orbs at the edge for Sephirot's. Those orbs gradually grow, so keep away. Share stack markers and dodge other attacks.

Before Boss 3
Minotaurs break through some walls. Several break quickly, while another merely threatens to.

The Ultima Beast
Raised arms mean move away; standing upright means move beneath it. A marked player receives eight-direction arrow beams; others stay away from that ring, with distance making the gaps easier to use.
A white outward-arrow marker on the tank is proximity damage. Everyone else moves far from the tank. Later these mechanics overlap; watch animations and stay calm.
286:
Sigmascape V1.0

The boss has no facing for melee positionals. For proximity attacks, more than half the arena's length is normally enough distance unless badly undergeared.
Spotlights remove ghosts but also hurt players. Once a spotlight fixes and a magic circle appears, leave the circle. For four blocking ghosts, clearing one near the front gives more room. Tethered players kite their ghost in a sufficiently wide circle to keep it nearly still; the spotlight target places the light on it. Untethered players may touch that ghost.
Avoid ghosts entering from the train's sides. Contact sends you into a private room where you must kill a ghost to escape, costing damage uptime.
Two proximity-marker targets move to the far rear; when markers disappear they return immediately. Others keep attacking normally.
During adds, a carriage draws alongside. Kill its enemies, use the transfer point, and run forward to destroy the smokestack. After returning, each player must touch a separate ghost to enter a carriage; staying outside causes suffocation.
After leaving the rooms, enmity resets. The main tank re-establishes aggro.
Later, handle Acid Rain with tethered ghosts normally and heal anyone clipped by spotlights. When ghosts overlap the train's rear collision knockback, move backward early so the knockback does not throw you into a ghost.
287:
Sigmascape V2.0

Four paintings stand in the corners, each with another painting on the floor before it. Stand on a floor painting and use the duty action to gain the corresponding mechanic effect.
The boss appears slightly after combat begins, which matters for timed openers. It has no positionals.
Fire painting: use its floor painting for fire resistance. Do not paint too early: damage happens only after the boss finishes casting, flies to the painting and speaks.
Rock painting: use it to ride a plane over Earthquake. This resolves as the boss arrives, earlier than fire. Two players also get pursuing AoEs and should circle outside, away from the party.
Water painting: one player activates it to raise a rock. Everyone hides behind the rock from the wave. The wave arrives late, so do not raise the rock too early.
Wind painting: everyone gathers in that corner. One player, usually a healer, becomes Typhon and blows away the nearby wind orbs. Clear only the two or three near the party; there is time for at most three. Then handle separation tethers and a stack.
Water plus fire: activate fire first, then raise the water painting's rock.
Fire plus rock: activate fire first, then board the plane at the rock painting.
Raidwides and tankbusters occur around each painting sequence. Tanks mitigate and healers recover the party.
288:
Sigmascape V3.0

Watch the background monitor; it determines the special mechanics. The boss also uses tankbusters and raidwides. Dodge the unmarked frontal Magitek Ray when its cast begins. Red overhead markers do not require leaving the party; use personal mitigation if available and heal the damage.
When the boss loads a monitor: 
Dadaluma: a raidwide knockback, preventable with knockback immunity, is followed by eight chakra circles. Occupy one per player; the main tank can center the boss, with four melee taking inner circles and four ranged taking outer ones. The off-tank holds Dadaluma when he appears. Watch the boss's frontal laser while killing him.
Bibliotaph: extinguish the magic circles with three players in each, in sequence. The off-tank collects the book add. Dodge the boss's laser and heal while killing it.
Ultros: dodge circles under marked players, heal the raidwide and avoid tentacle line attacks. The off-tank collects Ultros. When the boss flies and strafes toward random players, watch its facing and take Ultros out of the firing path.
Air Force: leave the boss's point-blank AoE. If an aircraft add appears, the off-tank brings it beneath the boss to kill it. Watch approaching missiles and use the gaps.
Two bombs then fall. Wait about three seconds for their countdowns and colored glowing fuses. Step on the fuse matching the countdown's color to defuse each. Players who do not know the mechanic should not step randomly on fuses. Tanks may reposition the boss if bombs land beside the party.
289:
Sigmascape V4.0

Mark north to keep orientation. There are no rails, so you can fall. Hyperdrive is a small-area main-tank tankbuster; others keep clear.
Blue orbs around Kefka mean his warnings are truthful: avoid marked areas. Red question-mark orbs mean the warnings lie: stand on the question-marked ground. Fire spread/stack markers also invert: obey truthful ones, but stack for false spreads and spread for false stacks.
For Graven Image, a statue rises north. At HP thresholds the platform rises to the next statue; its mechanic follows each cast.
First statue: a wind orb appears on a side. Once the rectangular AoE warning appears, stand beneath the orb for knockback, or use immunity. It may switch hands, so do not commit early.
Second statue: avoid the half with the yellow or black orbs.
Third statue: look away from a purple eye, but face a yellow eye with a red question mark. Handle Kefka's own mechanics simultaneously.
When two dark circles appear for his teleport, stand on the outer side of the edge circle. He teleports there and may fire a 150-degree cone inward. The circles and teleport effect themselves do no damage.
His wind cast knocks back from his position. Knockback prevention works, but watch its cooldown because knockbacks are frequent.
290:
the Jade Stoa

DPS dodge visible attacks. When the tiger add appears and the tank receives a large white outward-arrow proximity marker, move far from that tank.
Healers prepare for raidwides and the tankbuster. The tiger's cleaves also hit hard. Its final long cast deals damage according to its remaining HP, so mitigate more if the party has not lowered it enough.
The main tank keeps Byakko central facing away and mitigates the tankbuster. Unlike Extreme, the normal tiger add need not be taken away by the off-tank; tanks can agree who handles it. Whoever tanks it must mitigate.
Everyone shares stack markers and avoids red, yellow and black ground hazards.
The airborne phase is a bullet-dodging game. Use a high camera angle to avoid orbs from below, stay close to the boss for the spinning kick and avoid horizontal dives. The boundary is instantly lethal.
Later, lightning circles advance in two sets: first a cross, then an X. Wait outside the X lanes. After the first cross set has exploded twice, move sideways into the space behind those advancing circles to avoid the second set.
291:
the Jade Stoa (Extreme)

Assign two groups: MT/H1/D1/D2 and ST/H2/D3/D4. For later purple circles, common positions are tanks north, healers southwest and DPS southeast.

Phase 1
Byakko grabs and throws the current main tank for a stack, resets that tank's enmity, then grabs the new highest-enmity player for another stack. Each stack gives Physical Vulnerability Up. Normally the off-tank provokes as the first tank is grabbed; the main-tank group shares first, then the off-tank group shares on the other side. Better gear may allow a tank to solo with full mitigation or invulnerability; agree beforehand.
During bullet patterns, three players receive a wind debuff. They must stay apart from one another or damage the whole raid.
The off-tank takes the summoned tiger. Two marked players place three successive sludge puddles at the edge, not centrally. Move the tiger to the opposite side and focus it, especially if damage is low.
A proximity attack targets the off-tank as the tiger flies; others shelter beneath Byakko. Immediately afterward dodge the tiger's line toward the party. After two AoEs, Byakko flies away and the tiger returns centrally. Everyone attacks it while ranged and healers intercept edge orbs. There is heavy damage throughout, and the off-tank is far from the party, so heal carefully. The tiger's final AoE scales with its remaining HP.

Phases 2 and 3
In the aerial phase, use movement keys to dodge orbs, wind circles and lines.
After the heavy landing raidwide, handle advancing cross then X lightning circles. Start in a gap between the later lanes; once the first set advances through two explosions, move behind it into its vacated gap.
The throw-and-stack returns; tanks may solo with invulnerability. Immediately afterward, move behind the boss for an unmarked 270-degree spinning kick.
During later bullets, three growing circles go to the assigned role positions: tank north, healer southwest, DPS southeast. Overlaps cause dangerous raidwide damage.
The later tiger is commonly left alive and its final attack handled with tank Limit Break 3 near the end of the cast, after the second preceding raidwide. This source's exact timing depends on the Chinese cast-bar text; use the agreed encounter timing rather than that text cue.
474:
the Great Hunt

This Monster Hunter crossover works differently from normal encounters. Rathalos has no cast bars or conventional enmity; watch its animations. In the final phase, normal healing stops working and you must use Mega-Potions. Their drinking animation takes longer than a normal item use.
Roar then charge: it stretches its head toward a player, roars and immediately charges. Dodge sideways.
Bite and tail: it tilts its neck sideways before biting in front and sweeping its tail.
Fire: it raises its neck and marks a player with a fire circle. Bait this onto adds when possible.
Melee are generally safest behind its left heel.
During adds, a tank gathers enemies beneath Rathalos. Marked players can aim its attacks onto the group of enemies.
A large bull then stuns Rathalos. One player interacts in front of the head to mount it; everyone else kills the bull before time expires. Tank the bull facing away because it cleaves. Healers also watch the mounted player's HP. Hide behind the bull's corpse from Rathalos's transition fire.
Final phase: everyone receives the effect preventing normal healing. Rathalos flies, takes reduced damage, charges without the earlier warning and uses a frontal fire cone. Always avoid its front.
After sufficient damage it falls, takes increased damage and its tail becomes targetable. Cutting the tail deals enormous damage. Prefer attacking the body first and cutting the tail near the end of the knockdown window.
After victory, manually carve the scales before leaving.
475:
the Great Hunt (Extreme)

The party has four players. As in normal mode, watch Rathalos's animations rather than cast bars. Three total knockouts fail the encounter and restart it.
It adds a repeated right-side half-circle tail sweep, signaled by lowering its head and raising its rear. Dodge both consecutive sweeps. It can also jump backward and breathe fire; avoid its front. Behind the left heel is generally safest.
The main tank gathers and kills adds, preferably beneath the boss so marked fire attacks also hit them. The midfight bull has a painful frontal cleave; face it away. Healers watch the mounted player's HP.
In the final phase, gather behind Rathalos. Two players are enough to share the stack attack. It leaves fire, so place it near the edge. Healers cannot restore HP normally but can still cleanse debuffs.
When Rathalos falls it takes extra damage; use burst attacks. Delay cutting the tail until later in the knockdown, or until the second knockdown, because cutting it makes Rathalos rise immediately and ends the vulnerable damage window.
536:
the Swallow's Compass

This Four Lords quest dungeon features the Monkey King; its cloud also resembles a purchasable mount.

Before Boss 1
Turn right and clear three geomancer groups. The first creates a water orb near the rear-center; tanks can gather enemies near it for area damage. Destroy it promptly or its explosion removes roughly half the party's HP. Dodge later effects despite the bright visuals.

Otengu
Fireballs rotate clockwise or counterclockwise around the center. The outer side of the green decorative ring is relatively safe. Every collision gives vulnerability; two stacks can make later AoEs fatal. Look away whenever the boss displays a gaze eye.

Before Boss 2
Waterfalls cover the passage with knockback AoEs. Tanks can shelter behind low walls, which also catch knocked-back players. The damage itself is not especially high.

Daidarabotchi
Stay fairly close. When it raises a hand, move immediately to the other side. Marked DPS keep moving: five stone pillars erupt consecutively, but only the first has a ground marker.
After it creates a central pool, favor the front half to keep space for cone dodges. The water expands; do not enter it.

Before Boss 3
Birds and bears hit very hard. Avoid a full pull without suitable gear and execution. Circular AoEs apply vulnerability to both enemies and players, so position carefully.

Qitian Dasheng
Watch the staff during the spinning attack. If it is very long and sparking, move close to the boss. If shorter without effects, move away.
Later, two copies cast together; shelter beneath the one with the sparking staff. The staff thrust is a painful tankbuster: mitigate and heal promptly.
537:
Castrum Fluminis

Torment is an early heavy frontal tankbuster. Tanks mitigate; healers prioritize recovery and others stay away from the tank.
Fans fall from the middle outward. Start at the edge, preferably by the last fan to land. Once the central fan's attack animates and disappears, move centrally to avoid the outer fans. Dodge the spear attack; share the gun attack in its line. Kill summoned adds promptly.
During the add phase, tanks collect enemies; tethered adds have no normal enmity. After the final add, prepare raidwide mitigation. Slower add kills make the transition damage higher and can cause a wipe.
In the final phase, the arena splits black and white. Each side builds its corresponding moon debuff, roughly every four or five seconds. At five stacks, Doom and a powerful damage-over-time effect are applied; even clearing Doom by leaving may not save you from the damage. Move between colors before reaching five. Melee can cross the dividing line; ranged and healers must track stacks and move between casts. If the floor colors do not render, the source suggests checking graphics drivers or restarting.
Two orbs also create donut attacks. Stand close to an orb or outside its ring rather than in the damaging band. Earlier mechanics continue: frontal tankbuster, raidwide, fans, spear or gun, and tethered adds.
The repeated stack attack requires everyone to remain together for multiple hits. Healers sustain recovery, using faster or instant healing if needed, and tanks can add party mitigation. Left/right blade casts have clear warnings in normal mode; dodge the indicated half. Extreme uses the same areas without those warnings.
538:
the Minstrel's Ballad: Tsukuyomi's Pain

Guide under construction. The source also lists external written and video guides and a practice simulator.
539:
the Weapon's Refrain (Ultimate)

The source lists external guides rather than an in-plugin walkthrough.
550:
the Ridorana Lighthouse

Famfrit
Watch the jug when he raises it overhead: its opening determines the cone's direction. Avoid that side; healers can help players who misread it.
His straight-path jug call sends three jugs across the arena's diameter. His curved-path call sends three circling jugs, rotating clockwise, counterclockwise and clockwise. Dodge their paths.
Red inverted-triangle targets must group with at least one other player. Being alone causes knockback and vulnerability.

Before Boss 2
The large-headed bomb enemies explode in sizable areas on death. Do not gather all nine and kill them simultaneously or the raid can wipe.

Belias
Stand on slow-moving clocks. After the fast clocks explode, move onto their cleared positions before the slow ones explode.
When he prepares a corner charge, a floor tile on the route shows an arrow. He turns at that tile and charges along the arrow; predict both legs.
Clock-hand tether targets stand at the edge and remain still. Passing the tether through other players petrifies them.
Separate the three adds so they do not tether.
After adds, four pointers land. Each circle contains a smaller arrow. Stepping on its circle rotates that arrow 90 degrees; rotate all small arrows to face outward.

Before Boss 3
The edge enemies remain stationary until their casts finish; a ranged Limit Break can clear them. The second wave becomes invulnerable and tethers to an ancient device: destroy the device first.

Construct 7
Some attacks have no ground warning. Prepare for addition with totals up to thirteen.
Dispose is a point-blank AoE: move away. The frontal cleaning barrage rotates along the displayed arrows; stay close and follow it quickly.
Subtract reduces your HP to a single-digit number. For the subsequent arithmetic cast, add a circle's number to your HP to meet the condition. For example, with HP 3 and a requirement for a multiple of four, use the circle marked 1. With HP 8, stand outside all circles. The answer is checked at cast completion. Correct answers grant a beneficial status; wrong ones grant a penalty.
After arithmetic, HP returns to normal; heal everyone immediately before the raidwide.
Each party's add arena differs: A has polarity tethers and linked players separate; B dodges slow incoming missiles; C handles Acceleration Bomb by stopping actions, auto-attacks and movement when the timer ends.
After adds, the red empowered boss casts faster and marks more players. Sprint helps keep up with the rotating barrage.

Yiazmat
Mark A/B/C at 2, 6 and 10 o'clock for adds. Keep the boss central. Its tankbuster is a circle around the tank; others keep away.
Raised forelegs signal a frontal petrification cone; avoid that facing.
Magnetic Lysis divides the floor into positive and negative areas and gives players polarity. Stand on the opposite polarity to be held down. Resolve overlapping mechanics first, then return to the correct floor. Floating polarity symbols signal imminent resolution; the wrong side can throw you out of the arena. Heal the raid.
Follow the multi-part claw charges, including turns. Separate tethered adds because they become invulnerable when close.
584:
Saint Mocianne's Arboretum (Hard)

The garden is now flooded with mud.

Before Boss 1
Look away from gaze markers.

Nullchu
Mitigate the heavy tank hit. A marked player places their attack away from both boss and adds, then moves once the marker disappears. A stack follows; gather behind the boss.
For Devour, watch the add the boss will jump to. Prepare to move toward that add; after eating it, the boss turns and repeatedly attacks a half-arena. Stay out until the animation fully finishes.

Before Boss 2
The large tree's dark-circle attack turns targets into leaf creatures. Avoid it yourself, but let it hit mud enemies to remove their damage-reduction buff and greatly lower their attacks. The cast can be interrupted if appropriate.

Lakhamu
Conveyors push players about half the arena in their arrow direction when the cast ends. Edge golems also attack. Usually stand near the edge of a conveyor without a golem.
Earthquake requires moving away then back close, though ranged can stay very far out. The two Earthshaker targets separate left and right rather than lining up. Damage is otherwise modest.

Before Boss 3
Open sluices to wash off enemy damage-reduction buffs. Tanks position enemies underneath; the large dragon turtle may need extra adjustment because of its hitbox.

Tokkapchi
Four solid green tiles interrupt the grated floor. When mud surges from below, stand on solid green tiles. When marked falling mud circles appear, stand on grating so it drops through. A circle may partially cover green as long as the player is on grating.
Any action with initial direct damage knocks the mud-ball add. Push it onto solid green ground and protect it from mud below, falling mud, the boss and add attacks. Two mud hits make it explode for near-wipe damage, survivable only with heavy group mitigation. Left safely alone, it eventually causes only a smaller raidwide explosion.
585:
the Burn

Experienced groups should find the pacing familiar.

Before Boss 1
With suitable previous-tier equipment, a full pull is manageable. Falling rocks deal roughly half HP and use a different warning from the usual orange circle. Enemies can also be hit by rocks, but gain no vulnerability; do not risk players for minor extra damage when area damage is already strong. Tanks may instead pull into clear ground.

Hedetet
Mitigate the tankbuster. Marked players and everyone targeted by the raidwide hide behind pillars. When all players receive circular markers, keep those circles off the pillars or they break.

Before Boss 2
The large square locomotive enemies hit hard and cleave in front. Tanks mitigate and face them away.

Defective Drone
Place poison markers at the edge. When the boss disappears to one side, watch the incoming robots from the center. The smoking robot without three overhead bars marks the safe lane. Heal players knocked toward the edge.
Gears cross from the long edges; avoid their lanes. If robot lanes, gears and a locomotive add overlap, find the robot lane first, then check gears. Tank the locomotive while others continue attacking the boss.

Before Boss 3
Sand rising from the ground is only a visual warning of hidden enemies; you cannot bypass them. Tanks collect them.

Mist Dragon
Blue markers create ice: the tank's arrow places one circle forward and three behind, while other markers leave a straight line. Place these near the edge to preserve space. Healers prepare cleanses and healing, because the damage and damage-over-time effect are severe.
Radiant mist creates cross-and-diagonal rays centered on a random player. Watch the target and move early; waiting for ground markers can be too late.
When the boss disperses, three adds appear and the central boss has an AoE marker. Do not attack the boss then or become frozen. Direct-damage actions free frozen teammates.
During Deep Fog, Sprint around the edge to locate the dragon and reveal its dive warning. If you cannot find it after half a circuit, spread opposite teammates or stay away from the center. Free and heal frozen players immediately.
587:
Alphascape V1.0

Keep the boss central for the opening attacks. Element phases work as follows.
Water: water covers the sides. Everyone gathers beneath the boss to place donut attacks without removing all safe space. After two resolutions, two proximity markers go to opposite edges. Their water orbs then create tethers; the two tanks each intercept one, front and back, using mitigation.
Earth: tank the boss at the far north and mitigate the heavy damage. Two knockbacks can be prevented. Then divide into two stacks beside the boss; each stack hits twice, and nobody should take both groups' hits. Dodge the remaining attacks.
Fire: only the center remains safe. Two rounds of individual small circles are placed toward the outside, then two groups stack beside the boss. Dodge the later attacks.
Wind: a central tornado appears. Move the boss northwest early and follow it. Handle the knockback with immunity or by standing close to the tornado along a diagonal. Immediately shelter behind the boss from the huge following AoE. After the second knockback, healers receive proximity markers and place them left and right; tanks take the resulting tethers.
After either water/earth or fire/wind, the boss returns centrally and Deep Pain reduces everyone to one HP. Heal immediately. Dodge familiar attacks, preferably placing donuts together, while destroying the central dark crystal. Its defeat triggers a transition raidwide.
The second half uses whichever elemental pair did not appear first. With sufficient damage, the final element may be skipped.
588:
Alphascape V2.0

Keep Midgardsormr central. Watch the two rotations to predict the AoE. Horizontal then horizontal means move away. Horizontal then vertical means stand beneath his hitbox. Vertical then vertical means stand diagonally, between the cross attacks aligned with his facing. If he is angled, the cross is angled too. Vertical then horizontal appears only in Savage.
Four marked players spread apart; unmarked players avoid lines from the boss through them.
Akh Morn targets one player with four heavy shared hits. Gather and heal; a tank target may solo with invulnerability. Ahk Rhai places repeated attacks at random players' positions; move as soon as the cast ends.
After the transition, avoid a north-origin dive and fireballs. A small dragon and pillars appear. Main tank takes the dragon to an edge facing outward while everyone destroys all pillars to remove its invulnerability. Then kill it, avoiding its frequent frontal cones and healing the tank.
Dodge the other visible mechanics.
589:
Alphascape V3.0

Keep Omega central.
For left/right Wave Cannon, dodge the named side. Omega then turns 180 degrees and casts again before turning back. If the second name matches the first, cross through the boss; if different, remain where you were.
Red circle markers leave lava while line lasers also fire. Spread and place them at the edge.
Peripheral Synthesis creates small fists advancing inward. Target them and use the Omega Jammer duty action.
During the transition, blue floor in the center and outer ring is instantly lethal. Attack the central monitor while occupying circles. First there are eight: tanks/melee take four inner ones and healers/ranged four outer ones. Then four appear; each needs at least one player.
The first circle set grants substantial Limit Break gauge; a melee LB can be used because more gauge follows. After defeating the simulation, repeatedly use Omega Jammer on the central projection point to raise a barrier.
Later Peripheral Synthesis may create a large fist firing a frontal line. Larger and smaller fists can overlap; distinguish their attacks.
A random tether target goes far away from the party. The tether transfers, so others must not intercept accidentally; the attack's area is very large. Healers dispel Paralysis from anyone hit.
590:
Alphascape V4.0

Keep the boss central. Early individual markers are followed by a stack, so do not run too far.
The first transformation knocks back, preventable with immunity, then markers are followed by crosses; spread well.
The next transformation uses a huge point-blank AoE. Move away, then handle individual markers and a stack like the opening while a donut requires moving beneath the boss.
When the boss dissolves again, one player gets a stack and another a pink circle. Place the solo circle at the edge and share centrally. The central landing then knocks back while the solo position explodes; knockback prevention is recommended.
A central boss raises a wing-like shield to protect a casting boss behind it. Destroy the shield bearer, then the other caster, or wipe.
After another marker-placement sequence, players receive Program M or Program F. Program M stays and attacks the central target; Program F goes to the edge target. The wrong target takes no damage. Tanks separate the two bosses; their later proximity-resonance buff makes them extremely strong if tethered together.
Frequent AoEs and tank hits continue. Keep party HP safe. Once one boss dies, the survivor repeatedly casts raidwides; finish it quickly.
595:
Kugane Ohashi

Tankbusters are frontal cones; face the boss away and mitigate. Gather for the opening butterfly cast, then leave once butterflies fall because a huge circle follows.
After the transition, dodge checkerboard lines, individual markers and donuts. With shields/mitigation, two or three melee can place their circles together, as can both tanks; ranged place theirs away. Donuts form centered on those positions. At full HP, one donut hit can be survived if no safe route exists.
For red inverted-triangle markers, gather behind the boss with another player rather than standing alone.
Both tanks later get proximity markers and move into separate corners. The boss splits; each tank holds one copy facing outward with mitigation. Heal them and preferably kill the main tank's copy first because their cooldowns may be lower.
After a raidwide, a proximity marker targets the main tank. The boss jumps there; everyone then follows, since lightning orbs cover other areas.
After the orbs explode, four players are captured. Targets move away from the boss while others break their chains. Grouping captured players together allows a physical ranged Limit Break to help. Free everyone before the gaol cast ends or they die.
A later attack reduces the whole party to one HP. Stay close for healing. For the wave attack, dodge to the sides first, then enter the central gap after its initial hit. Later mechanics combine earlier ones; keep the boss central.
596:
Hells' Kier

Keep Suzaku central and mitigate the early tankbuster.
When small birds appear, everyone brings them beneath the boss and kills them centrally. Tethered ranged players must also come close. After the raidwide, immediately destroy the central resurrection feather. A feather explosion reaching a bird corpse revives it at full HP with buffs; revived birds must die promptly or self-destruct. A tank hit overlaps the feather phase.
In the next phase, each player stands on one of eight small circles around the lotus pattern. Turn your character, not merely the camera, to match the circle's arrow. Light and sound confirm the facing. A high camera helps. Intercept incoming orbs while facing correctly to gain Damage Up; incorrect facing feeds Suzaku and increases her damage instead.
The transition raidwide follows. Stay off the central red floor: it becomes a hole afterward.
For the pull melody, move away; for the push melody, move close. Both have a flute sound and can be resisted with knockback prevention.
The repeated kicking tankbuster is followed by a180-degree AoE. The tank mitigates heavily and moves toward the boss's side; healers prepare.
For the floor sequence, four sectors display symbols and matching colored orbs sit outside. A tethered bird circles clockwise or counterclockwise. When it reaches an orb, that orb's matching floor sector explodes. Watch the correspondence and the bird.
The first sequence has one-to-one symbols. Later four orbs appear together and sectors explode in succession, with circular or crossing patterns. Follow the sequence carefully; if necessary one floor hit can be survived with healing.
Raidwides, tower/spread circles and lines overlap the floor sequence, melodies or kicks. Stay calm and resolve the combined mechanics.
597:
Hells' Kier (Extreme)

Guide under construction. The source also lists external written and video guides.
611:
the Ghimlyt Dark

Many familiar NPCs join this battlefield.

Before Boss 1
Choose pull sizes to suit the party; no special mechanics are noted.

Mark III-B Magitek Colossus
Dodge attacks and face the frontal tankbuster away. When it returns centrally for Magitek Slash, a cone and rotating arrows show the sweep direction. Start beside the cone on the side opposite the arrows. Each slash leaves damaging fire. Stay fairly close to correct positioning quickly if you choose the wrong side.

Before Boss 2
Large enemies hit harder; mitigate and heal.

Prometheus
Stay close for the early huge AoE. When it burrows, watch the outer rock wall for a glowing red section. A line attack comes from there; move to either side of that line and wait through the sustained laser before returning. Later proximity damage overlaps the laser; avoiding the laser takes priority.

Before Boss 3
Kan-E-Senna raises a barrier during the final large enemy's cast; enter it. An NPC Limit Break delivers the final blow, but keep attacking: it cannot kill the enemy from full HP.

Annia and Julia
Either sister can be attacked first. Dodge attacks and spread unavoidable markers without overlap. Each defeated sister triggers a combined attack with very thin yellow trajectory lines; the edge is often safer. Finally both appear and cast their enrage together. A caster or physical ranged Limit Break can help finish them.
636:
the Orbonne Monastery

Before Boss 1
Look away from the trash gaze or receive dispellable Doom.

Mustadio
The arena is effectively a four-by-four grid. Yellow tethers activate outer enemies, which attack their corresponding rows or columns. Blue tethers activate inner enemies, each covering the two-by-two square beneath it.
Analysis sends Mustadio onto a high outer platform. Players receive an unanalysed side, also shown as a gap in a golden C-shaped ring. Turn that gap directly toward him or die. He first appears northeast and later chooses randomly. Spreading out makes each player's gap easier to see.

Agrias
Sword and shield circles grant special actions. For the shield-required attack, pick up a shield, face Agrias and use it, then remain still. Moving or facing wrongly invalidates the protection.
In the isolated room, attack unmarked enemies normally. For shielded enemies, take a sword circle and use its special attack. There is brief invulnerability after returning. Place ordinary markers together when possible.
Add phase: parties A and C each take a northern add and use shields for its AoE. Party B handles the southern add. When sword circles appear, use swords to destroy its tethered enemies before continuing.
The final tether-plus-marker attack can be blocked with the shield; surviving it without a shield requires healing.

Before Boss 3
The second trash wave has magic circles. Occupy each with the number of players shown by its dots.

Thunder God
Party B starts at the entrance, A at 10 o'clock and C at 2 o'clock. Take positions before pulling.
Doom reduces everyone to one HP. Heal each player to full to remove it; stay in healer range.
Watch the swords: held horizontally outward means avoid the pointed circular platform; planted into the ground means move close inside the hitbox; raised overhead means move outward beyond the circular platform.
A large red-black marker goes to one side of your party's area.
The tank attack applies four physical-vulnerability stacks before a heavy hit. Tanks mitigate. The source notes the vulnerability can be dispelled after all four stacks, reducing the final damage.
For the dark circles on either side of each party's platform, put at least three players into each of your two circles.
A pursuing red-black marker becomes an orange circle once locked. Run continuously away without entering others' paths; taking two hits is generally fatal.
During adds, tanks face enemies outward. Place markers toward the add's outer side.
The first sword sequence after adds hits three platforms successively. Dodge and return promptly for another one-HP Doom that requires full healing.
A four-hit tether mechanic applies physical vulnerability with each hit. Healers and DPS pass it between different players; tanks do not take it. Taking two hits is fatal.

Ultima
Dodge attacks, including returning mechanics from earlier bosses. Three large crystals fall in order during Grand Cross and fire cardinal lasers; watch each.
For clocks, start on the slow pattern and move to the fast one's cleared position. Avoid falling towers. Group red inverted-triangle markers. When an edge boss has one fiery side, use the nonfiery half.
During the respite, raise fallen players quickly. Enter the allied barrier, use mitigation and heal continuously even inside it, while focusing the central add.
