687:
the Dying Gasp

Damage throughout this fight is high, and failed mechanics easily give Vulnerability Up. Healers should watch the entire party; players with excessive stacks may be difficult to keep alive.

The tankbuster is an AoE: everyone must stay away from the main tank. Early in the fight, purple weapons appear for the attack called Bad Faith; dodge toward a direction without weapons. The effect resembles a bard's Refulgent Arrow.

Dark red circles mark falling blue magic sigils. Their explosions extend beyond the visible blue sigils: the floor-pattern boundary shows the actual blast radius. There are nine positions, including the center; each explodes once, in a random order. Stay clear.

During the add phase, circular spread markers and a stack marker appear together. The circle-marked players move away, and everyone else stacks in the center.

After the adds die, a cutscene leads to a larger Hades at the arena edge. A red orb in front of him and a Shadow Stream cast signal a central blast; move to either side. Dual Strike hits the top two players on the enmity list very hard. The off-tank must hold second enmity so a DPS is not hit.

When Hades reaches one arm over the arena, stand outside that arm to avoid its laser. With both arms extended, stay in the center. The shadows on the floor can help identify the pattern. For the imprisonment cast, marked players separate: everyone inside a marked circle is trapped. Destroy the aetherial prisons before the subsequent chorus cast finishes, or the prisoners die. Trapping extra players leaves fewer people free to break the prisons.

When the arena darkens and everyone receives Doom, occupy all illuminated circles simultaneously to remove it. For arrows flowing across the floor, move toward their origin so the knockback pushes you safely across; knockback immunity works. Gold markers without circles bait cone AoEs when the markers disappear. These can overlap; bait them toward the edge, then dodge their telegraphs.

When chains trigger an Active Time Maneuver, press keys rapidly to escape; modifier keys such as Ctrl, Alt and Shift do not count.

The final repeated dark attacks deal raidwide damage, with a larger hit every fifth pulse. The arena is consumed progressively from the outside. On the third expansion, previously safe positions are also consumed; standing in them applies Bleeding. Defeat Hades before his final enrage cast completes.
689:
Eden's Gate: Sepulture

The arena is a 4-by-4 grid. Most attacks resolve using these tiles.

Stonecrusher is a heavy main-tank hit with Physical Vulnerability Up. It can generally be healed through; tanks should discuss whether to swap.

Evil Earth spreads outward: one tile lights up, then its eight neighbors, then the next outer ring. Wait outside, then move inward as soon as the inner tiles explode.

When Titan announces that his shell will become gauntlets, the armor moves to his hands. First stand on the row of rocks in front of him to avoid the initial AoE; when the floor beneath you turns blue, dodge to a side. When he announces wheels instead, he becomes a vehicle. Stand on the wider safe side of his path, account for the knockback, and avoid the blue floor tiles.

Rock and bomb patterns:
- Two falling rocks with proximity markers: move to the edge to reduce the initial damage. One rock glows yellow and explodes. Hide behind the other rock for the next raidwide blast.
- Four corner bombs: one is tethered to Titan and grows larger. Stand at the midpoint of an edge away from that enlarged bomb. For a large southwest bomb, the north or east edge midpoint is safe.
- Three rows of bombs: rows land successively at grid intersections. Avoid the enlarged tethered bomb, start by the third row, then move to the first row after it explodes. Small explosions fit inside a 2-by-2-tile square, leaving several safe gaps.
- Cross followed by corner bombs: start in a corner to avoid the cross, then move inward after it explodes to avoid the corner bombs.

The two-rock and cross/corner patterns can overlap Evil Earth. With two rocks, resolve Evil Earth first. For the cross/corner pattern, move to a corner first, then watch Evil Earth's direction and adjust.

Earthen Fury applies a Sludge damage-over-time effect to the party. Healers should keep everyone healthy.

the Copied Factory

Many NieR attacks resolve on their animation, after the telegraph disappears. Wait for the animation before moving back into danger.

The source also links an official NieR promotional page; it contains an introduction rather than a walkthrough.

Boss 1: Serial-jointed Command Model
- The repeated frontal energy barrage targets a random player. Watch for sudden turns; stand to the side or rear to avoid it.
- Tethered guided attacks should be aimed outside the arena. Do not overlap your tether with another player's.
- Side/center rotating attacks show their AoE for less than a second after the cast. Preposition: side attacks require the center, and center attacks require the sides.
- Aerial units move while dropping circular AoEs. Keep moving or use the safe spot inside their spawn position at the crossing of two floor pipes. The original guide illustrates these positions with diagrams. The second occurrence includes a knockback; knockback immunity works.
- Dodge the remaining telegraphs normally.

Between bosses 1 and 2

Tanks in each alliance should pick up all enemies along the route; everyone else defeats them.

Boss 2: Hobbes

Each alliance is sent to its own arena. Both the floor and rotating surrounding walls have mechanics; watch the on-screen announcements. The source recommends gathering at the front-right of the arena.
- The laser-resistance test deals substantial raidwide damage. Mitigate and heal.
- Ring lasers expand slowly with unusual telegraphs. Avoid the first ring, then move outside the remaining rings' path.
- When wall flamethrowers activate, look behind you for an inactive emitter. Their flames angle inward; emitters on both sides form an inverted V.
- When the wall's right arm activates, a blue circle appears in the center followed by three consecutive AoE sets. Rotate in the central arrow's direction.
- When the wall's left arm activates, a container appears and its four walls fall outward. Dodge the falling panels at the front-right, then have one tank take both tethers away from the group for the small explosions. If no tank does so, tethered players must position sensibly away from others.
- Each alliance also handles its own floor hazards. Alliance B has forced movement; avoid being moved off the edge.

Between bosses 2 and 3
- Large tank: for the donut attack, wait for the pink orbs before moving. Tethered players must not drag an orb into the group; overlapping two explosions is lethal.
- Flight unit: a tether baits a sequence of advancing AoEs. Once the marker disappears, move sideways out of the line. Others stay clear of that direction.

Boss 3: Engels

Watch the boss's arms throughout. With one raised arm, move to the opposite side. With both raised, read the arm pattern; the original illustrated guide shows the first pattern on the first occurrence and the second on the next, with later patterns random.

Take marked attacks away from others. A yellow-arrow tracking marker produces multiple hits; do not return early.

When a charged chest laser accompanies twelve towers, the laser covers the middle six. Enter those towers immediately after the laser ends; every tower needs a player.

During adds, tanks hold the large enemies facing outward. 2P destroys the small ones. After the adds, everyone must gather in the southern half before being launched to another platform; elsewhere you can be crushed or fall.

On the new platform, mechanical arms sweep inward three times. Watch their positions and dodge; then handle the remaining telegraphs.

Boss 4: 9S-operated Walking Fortress
- Dodge the frontal main-cannon laser aimed at a random player.
- Front/rear volleys require the sides; side volleys require front or rear positions.
- When 9S undocks into a flight unit, he bombs one-third of the arena's width from an edge. 2P moves to the far end of the bombing route beforehand; marking her can help you find it. Bombing resolves on the smoke animation, so do not move back early.

714:
Anamnesis Anyder

Approach to boss 1

Fight several waves on the initial platform. When the boat stops, disembark on the right to reach the first boss.

Boss 1: Unknown

The boss's circular attack uses a rotating arrow beneath it. The arrow's initial stopping direction is not the final danger direction: the AoE follows its direction when the observation cast finishes. Do not decide the safe spot too early.

The second observation includes a clone and a stack. There is enough time to resolve the stack first and then find the safe area. Both the boss and its clone also cast frontal line AoEs, signaled by red energy at the head/mouth; move aside.

Between bosses 1 and 2: large pulls can pressure the tank. Choose a pace suited to the party.

Boss 2: Kyklops

Move away when he crouches for the large circular swing. Avoid the front when he raises an arm for the sweep. Move close when he crouches for the eye-of-the-storm donut attack.

Hammer and sword symbols appear successively on the tiles. The first symbol detonates first: stand on the other symbol, then move to the first tiles after their damage animation. Reverse this when the order reverses. The second hammer/sword set also has a stack or spreads; resolve those first.

Between bosses 2 and 3: prioritize enemies tethered to crystals. They cannot be stunned or interrupted, and their completed casts make the crystals summon more enemies.

Boss 3: Rukshs Dheem

After the boss jumps to an edge and performs the underwater ritual, a water channel forms across the center. Hands emerge and attack forward; stand behind the hands.

Four of the eight grates bubble while the boss returns to the center and repeats the ritual. Occupy the bubbling grates before the cast finishes to prevent adds from emerging and making the boss invulnerable. Tanks and melee should cover the nearer central grates; healers and ranged cover the distant corner grates.

Another ritual creates hands successively along the long edges. Their attacks resolve in spawn order. Start in a gap near the north/south areas, wait for the first side's hand animation, then cross to the cleared side. Sufficient mitigation and gear can allow surviving one hit, but dodging is preferable.

In the last version, all eight grates bubble and four hands appear at the sides. The hands cover nearby grates themselves, so players occupy the grates farther from the hands. Again, melee cover central positions and ranged cover corners. If adds emerge, defeat them to remove the boss's invulnerability.
715:
Eden's Verse: Fulmination

Passing through a lightning orb grants Surge Protection. Do not collect more after reaching three stacks: doing so causes the detrimental charged status and reduces healing received. When Ramuh charges lightning, signaled by his spinning hands and electrical effect, ensure you have at least one protection stack. Maintaining one or two beforehand can make this easier.

For the weapon-summoning mechanic, two or four lightning rods appear. Long rods produce very large circular AoEs; short rods do not. Hide behind a short rod. With four rods, use a corner.

For the phantom-summoning mechanic, read the lanes. With one phantom in the middle, stand close to the central solid line to survive the outward knockback, but never in the central charge lane. With three phantoms along the edge, use the lane without a phantom.

Thundercloud marks two players in purple. Place the clouds near the edges and far apart from one another; nearby clouds merge into a larger thunderstorm. Once the markers disappear, leave the dropped clouds. They pulse untelegraphed AoEs, visible as electrical rings when they resolve. Stay away until the clouds vanish.

These mechanics combine later. Healers should watch party health throughout.

717:
Cinder Drift

Ruby Weapon frequently returns to the center facing south. The main tank can keep it in that position from the pull.

Phase 1

Ruby Claw creates eight branching cracks. After they finish extending, telegraphs appear: close to the boss along a long branch is safe, as is farther from the boss along a short branch. If the next cast liquefies the floor, stand on a branch to avoid sinking; this has no ordinary AoE telegraph. If the next cast detonates the cracks, move off the branches instead.

Ruby Ray is a frontal line as wide as the target ring, aimed at a random player. Everyone should avoid the front.

For the spiral-claw mechanic, the original diagram places the safe region beyond the circles' common tangent, on the left side of their shared chord. The source stresses learning this position before attempting Extreme.

High-powered guided lasers mark both healers for separate stacks. Tanks and DPS split between them; nobody should take both.

When the boss jumps to an edge for its charge, stand behind the arrow at its feet while facing it. The charge is angled rather than directly toward the center: stand on the other side of its facing, then keep running along the edge after it charges. In the central-charge version, start at the edge to the boss's front-left and run clockwise after the charge.

For guided lasers, first move beneath the boss to avoid the initial AoE, then spread for the individual markers.

Phase 2

After the transition, each tank picks up one of the two adds. DPS receive meteor-stream markers and spread; healers restore health. Ruby Claw hits the tank five times for heavy damage: use strong mitigation and follow-up healing.

After the adds, watch the meteor countdown and time mitigation for impact. Four comets later land around the arena; hide behind them for the following AoE.

Finally, four moving circular markers with arrows approach from the cardinal directions. A meteor lands on each marker's fifth step. Each needs one player to catch it. The source recommends tanks/healers soaking while DPS keep attacking, then raising healers before tanks.

The remaining sequence is repeated raidwide damage; healers maintain party health.

719:
Eden's Verse: Furor

Mark the cardinal directions to avoid losing your bearings.

Phase 1: Garuda

The opening storm attacks two 90-degree cones. Their faint telegraphs are easier to see with an overhead camera.

Two blue stack circles appear. Each must contain more than two players; otherwise its target is launched and killed. A large blue circle in the center causes knockback: stand just outside its edge, or use knockback immunity, and do not enter it.

For the close-range AoE with blue tethers, tethered players bait approximately 30-degree cones. Separate the tethers and keep other players out of them.

Vacuum Slash divides the arena with a red AoE. The resulting red-black central strip is unsafe. Three wind orbs appear on each half; find the unusually wide gap between two orbs, or between an orb and the edge, and stand there for the knockback.

Phase 2: Ifrit

The first fiery punch tethers the main tank and charges through the tether line. Everyone hit receives Lightheaded; a second hit causes Concussion. The tank stays near Ifrit to shorten the line, others avoid it, and tanks swap afterward.

Another punch gives one player three tethers. Two other players take one each, then all three spread the lines apart. This also applies Lightheaded. Untethered players should stand slightly away from Ifrit so they do not take overlapping charges.

The subsequent heavy main-tank hit launches a tank who still has Lightheaded. Make the earlier swap so the tank receiving it has no such debuff.

After the spark-explosion cast and jump, follow the boss beneath its new position to continue attacking.

Phase 3

Both bosses return and the arena splits again. Ifrit lands beside one wind orb; players on his side stand beneath him, while the other half handles the wind pattern normally. Other mechanics combine the earlier phases.

Use party mitigation when the bosses merge; the damage can kill DPS without it. Later mechanics repeat. Continue watching the faint storm telegraphs.

726:
Eden's Verse: Iconoclasm

The boss is stationary and has no facing requirements. Its large target ring covers roughly a quarter of the arena. Do not fall off the edges.

Phase 1

After the opening raidwide, the tankbuster tethers the main tank for a heavy line attack. The tank moves sideways away from the party and mitigates; everyone else avoids that line. This repeats later.

For the wave command, orbs appear in order along the front. The first set charges first. Start on the later set's side, then move into the first set's cleared lane. For example, if left appears first and right second, start right and cross left after its charge.

The second occurrence introduces portals but can still be handled in the front half. The third uses the full portal pattern: identify the first orbs, choose the correct left/right starting position, then check the color of their rear portal. Move forward/backward to align with a side portal of the opposite color. After the frontal orbs resolve, watch the side portals and adjust again. Actual colors/order vary; the source diagram is only an example.

Forced teleportation gives a forward, backward, left or right status. When it expires, you move in the indicated direction. The two subsequent stacks must be separated; taking both is lethal.

The night-raid command uses light/dark polarity instead of spawn order. Light-aspected players take black orbs; dark-aspected players take white orbs.

Phase 2

Adds combine forced teleportation with in/out attacks. Check the teleport direction carefully so you do not fall.

Phase 3

Earlier mechanics return with additions. Teleportation now accompanies towers at the front/rear. Aim for the center of those ends so you can return promptly.

For night-raid side portals, choose the opposite color from the portal behind your initial column: if that rear portal is red, align with a blue side portal, and vice versa. These commands are the likeliest source of mistakes and deaths; healers should be ready.

728:
Eden's Verse: Refulgence

Mark the cardinal directions and watch the arena edges: you can fall.

Phase 1

The outfit-change cast has two variants. The first always requires looking away, indicated by a red eye above the tall boss. Moving close and facing away handles either variant.

Scythe Kick requires moving in; Axe Kick requires moving out. Read the cast name, because waiting for the telegraph can be too late. For the frost slash/thrust, slash is safe behind the boss and thrust is safe at the front-left/front-right; learn the cast names.

Diamond Dust: white-triangle targets place their AoEs in safe areas at the edge; yellow-circle targets separate in the middle. Four players then receive tracking AoEs: spread toward the edges and keep moving as the telegraphs follow.

The descending strike causes knockback. Use immunity, or avoid starting near an edge.

Mirrors repeat the boss's attacks. For the first reflected slash, dodge behind the boss, then go south away from the two mirrors. For a reflected thrust, dodge in front, then go north between the mirrors.

Phase 2: adds

Interrupt the earth sprite's Stoneskin with Interject. Lightning sprites reflect damage, so healers watch the attackers. Water sprites have more health but can be stunned; focus them. Intercept the tether from the sprite at the edge. If four adds reach the central crystal, including tethered ones, the party wipes.

Phase 3

Holy: one orb above the boss means the center is struck and the outer area is safe. Four orbs mean the outer areas are struck and the center is safe. The arena effects change accordingly.

The light-wave mechanic creates four towers, then two, then one. Two players are marked each time: they must bait their waves away from everyone and cannot take towers. The remaining towers require one, two and four players respectively. Resolve these quickly and calmly.

Mirrors now repeat the kicks. For Scythe Kick, start beneath the boss, then move beneath a mirror for its repeat. For Axe Kick, start away from the boss, then move toward the arena center for the repeat.

The final frozen-floor sequence combines two consecutive frost slash/thrust attacks. Manage your sliding carefully; the source suggests accepting one hit if necessary rather than losing control completely.

Repeated raidwides follow. Healers restore health, then finish the damage race after the transition.

736:
the Puppets' Bunker

Many NieR attacks resolve with their animation, after the warning disappears. Wait for the damage animation before returning. The source's official promotional page is an introduction, not a walkthrough.

Boss 1: 813P-operated Aegis Unit

Red-marked tanks move away from the party and mitigate. Other red-marked players also separate, then leave their position and return after the light pillar appears.

For the converging particle cannon's yellow areas, move into the area that shrinks fastest. When the overhead machinery rotates for the deflected cannon, hide behind the mechanical wing, away from its firing side.

During the final-song program, expanding yellow rings have gaps. Pass through the gaps and wait for each ground damage animation before moving to the next gap. Switch to adds promptly and dodge overlapping mechanics.

Between bosses 1 and 2

Group the platform enemies for a caster limit break. Each alliance tank should interrupt its large enemy's spreading-voltage cast. Agree on alliance ownership of left/middle/right enemies (ABC or BAC).

Purple-marked players place their circles away from enemies, near the outside, to avoid leaving fire under the melee group. Melee watch their feet.

Boss 2: 724P-, 767P- and 772P-operated Superior Flight Units

Alliances A/B/C are assigned left/middle/right automatically. Until one unit dies, you cannot damage another alliance's unit.

Aim the early line stacks outward to avoid striking another alliance. For the cooperative rotating slash, the three bosses form a triangle and extend blades along their movement paths. If your boss's blade is outside the triangle, go inside. If it is inside, stand directly behind your triangle vertex.

For the cooperative bombing sequence, advancing AoEs appear at an edge while the boss uses an out AoE. Start far from the boss and opposite the advancing AoEs' direction (if arrows point left, start to their right). As soon as the boss's AoE finishes, move in to avoid the other incoming AoEs.

For the cooperative charging slash, all three line up north. Dodge on the side without an extended blade; wait for the animation. If damage is slow, two bombs produce overlapping cross/diagonal AoEs. Moving far away is the simplest response.

Boss 3: 905P-operated Heavy Artillery Unit

When laser turrets activate, the central device shows high and low lights. Stand at the edge in the sector with the high light, then move into the neighboring sector as soon as its AoE resolves.

Two tanks are immediately marked for high-powered lasers. Separate and aim outward. Everyone else avoids both marked directions; the animation is clear and getting swept is lethal.

Random players receive concentrated-voltage markers. Spread without overlapping and avoid unnecessary movement; others adjust around them.

During the support-pod program, outer screens show R010 or R030. R010 is a line across the middle; R030 is a circle centered on its pod. Stand near the edge between two pods. For the later alternating R010/R030 pattern, use the gap between the pods linked to two adjacent R010 screens. Initially screens link to pods directly ahead; later they link diagonally, so follow the actual tethers.

Explosive compounds create yellow circles. On the first occurrence they turn blue with more than three players each; an insufficiently occupied circle causes raidwide damage. On the second occurrence, two players per circle suffice.

Between bosses 3 and 4

Dodge the many AoEs. Red laser lines indicate aiming only; the following yellow areas are the actual attacks. Damage resolves on animation, and failures apply Vulnerability Up.

Boss 4: Compound / Compound 2P

Red lights and tethers around the boss signal a donut: move beneath it. If the boss rotates with red lines, avoid those lines. When it vanishes to the edge, use its corresponding row/column to avoid the attack.

After transformation, read the sword stance during the charged blade attack:
- Crouched with sword raised: large circle; move out.
- Upright with sword behind the head: frontal cone; move to the side/rear.
- Upright with sword in the ground: donut; move in.

These attacks combine with teleportation. A tether's glowing endpoint shows the boss's destination; resolve the stance from that position.

After teleportation, the main tank keeps the boss near the edge. The three-hit stack also knocks back each time; aim the party toward the center to prevent being pushed off.

For the four-hit marked sequence, the boss jumps to player 1, cleaves toward 2, jumps to 3, then cleaves toward 4. Targets 1 and 3 stay still; 2 and 4 separate. Everyone else avoids the hits.

Clones repeat the charged sword attacks: first the central boss, then the four corner clones. Later towers combine with the same teleport rules. In the final teleport/line-AoE combination, two edge orbs teleport before firing across the arena; watch their destinations and dodge.

The source additionally cites susu's illustrated guide, Ziyan's video and a three-minute explanation video.
737:
the Heroes' Gauntlet

This main-scenario dungeon features returning allies.

Approach to boss 1

Tanks should bring enemies close to friendly NPCs so their AoEs help defeat them.

Boss 1: Spectral Thief

After the dash cast, an AoE and a destination tether appear. When all the green orbs around the boss disappear, it teleports to the tether endpoint and performs that AoE. Avoid the destination arrow.

Later, the clone dash uses two destinations. For circular AoEs, stay away from both arrows. For rectangular AoEs, choose a clear lane perpendicular to their orientation; for horizontal lines, move north/south to a row without an arrow.

Between bosses 1 and 2

Bring enemies into the friendly NPC's semicircular AoE, which turns them into frogs.

Boss 2: Spectral Necromancer

Stay close to dodge the initial random cones. Being hit applies dispellable Doom: a healer can use Esuna, or a bard can use the Warden's Paean.

Black holes spawn tethered enemies. Start together; when their tethers disappear, the tank moves the boss to an area without enemies. The abandoned enemies then explode in circles.

After the half-arena sludge, black circles under players spawn another set of tethered enemies. Spread: when they catch you, they bind you and cause a small AoE.

If a third tether sequence occurs, both enemy types are present. Spread and keep moving to place the first enemies and their stationary AoEs, then take the second enemies' small AoEs without overlapping others.

Between bosses 2 and 3

Hildibrand may appear among the allied NPCs. Near the end, a Spectral Paladin protects enemies behind it with Passage of Arms. Attack the front paladin and wait for the allied NPC limit break to break the protection before damaging the others.

Boss 3: Spectral Berserker

The corners turn white early; do not enter them. For a large blue circle at one side, stand close but outside it for the knockback, or use knockback immunity.

Afterward, spread the large markers to place rocks. The following individual stacks must be shared with those rocks.

When the boss jumps to the edge and telegraphs a full-arena attack, enter a crater left by the blue circle. Do not stay too long: its berserk buildup becomes full Berserk at eight stacks. When the boss raises and charges its axe, avoid its front.
738:
the Seat of Sacrifice

Some mechanics require special responses rather than simply dodging telegraphs. Healers should help players who fail mechanics while resolving their own safely.

The tankbuster is The Bitter End; the raidwide is Elddragon Dive.

Phase 1

About ten seconds into the fight, everyone's HP becomes 1 and True Walking Dead is applied. Heal each player to full to remove it. Stay near the healers and inside ground healing; gathering within the target ring from the pull helps.

For the light-sword attack, a glowing ring around the raised sword means move in; no ring means move out. Normal difficulty shows a telegraph; Extreme does not.

Absolute Fire III gives a red countdown and then three seconds of Pyretic. Stop actions, movement, turning and auto-attacks during Pyretic; deselect/sheath to prevent attacks. Absolute Blizzard III requires continued movement (jumping in place also works in the source's instructions), or you are frozen.

The imbued versions store fire or ice, then release it together with the sword attack. Remember whether to stop or move, then read the sword's in/out cue and satisfy both together.

A light draws a lethal triangle. Move outside its sloping lines. Immediately after it resolves, Bahamut dives from the north: move to the half without Bahamut. A tankbuster and raidwide follow.

Phase 2

Everyone must repeatedly press buttons until their restraint disappears in the Active Time Maneuver. One failure wipes the party. Keyboard, mouse and controller inputs count; using several fingers/buttons makes this easier than tapping with one finger.

Back in the arena, the boss charges four limit-break bars. A tank must use the party limit break about one second after the fourth bar fills, indicated by a sound. Healers can prepare shields/ground mitigation and heal afterward.

Phase 3

The boss gains True Hallowed Ground when a DPS starts a limit break. Use DPS limit breaks while the boss is already casting, or the damage is negated.

Remember the opening imbued fire/ice. Summoned black/white mages create four successive towers; at least two players occupy each. After the fourth, the sword attack resolves together with the stored fire/ice.

Dark knight/bard summons place two dark spots while Bahamut appears north. Use the quarter of the arena with neither a dark spot nor Bahamut. A proximity-marked player then takes the marker (white outward arrows) to a corner, while the others stack in the middle.

After a tankbuster, the boss uses limit breaks in order:
- LB1: three marked cone attacks; do not overlap.
- LB2: line stacks on both healers. Healers stand to opposite sides of the boss and the others split between them.
- LB3: four very large marked AoEs. Place them separately in the corners.

Two lights next draw triangles. Stay outside both, then immediately resolve the following fire/ice mechanic. After a raidwide, remember another stored imbued fire/ice.

The summoned ninja creates a water-column knockback from an edge. Use knockback immunity when the floor arrows appear, or start near the water column to be pushed across safely. Immediately stack with the party in the center. The sword attack then releases with the stored fire/ice; the timing is tight.

Four Bahamuts tether four players. Aim these tethers outward: their fire cones cover roughly 160 degrees.

After another tankbuster, two alternating sets of cones occur. Wait in a first-set safe area, then step sideways into a cleared first-set cone to avoid the second. Fire/ice resolves simultaneously with the second cones.

746:
Matoya's Relict

747:

Castrum Marinum

The rotating movement in phase 1 is the main challenge. Casters/healers can use instant casts; once familiar, they can fit a cast between movements. Phase 1 transitions when the boss reaches 0.1% HP.

Phase 1

After the initial tankbuster, rotating cones and expanding ring AoEs appear. Follow the cones in the direction of the arrows on the boss, keeping near a cone boundary, and step between the inside/outside of each expanding ring as it passes.

After the floor changes color, damage resolves when the white effect reaches the outer ring. Upright sigils fire lines forward and backward, so read their facing. For the left/right named sonic attack, move to the side named by the cast.

During the long cast with full-screen effects, dodge lethal floor AoEs. Cover appears during the latter half of the cast; hide behind it before the attack resolves.
787:
Ktisis Hyperboreia

Duty Support offers special companions and dialogue. The final boss has an interruptible cast: tanks and physical ranged should have Interject or Head Graze ready.

Approach to boss 1: two enemies spawn before the final door with AoE telegraphs; avoid their arrival damage.

Boss 1: Lyssa

When invisible, follow the footprints to the direction where they disappear. Story NPCs teleport, so simply following their movement is unreliable. Dodge the two icicle patterns as telegraphed.

Between bosses 1 and 2: large pulls are possible.

Boss 2: Ladon Lord

Each head breathes across 120 degrees: the middle head covers the front, left head covers left-rear, right head covers right-rear. Heads can turn before the attack; use their facing during the cast. Ctrl+Up can adjust the camera if heads are hard to see.

Fireball crosses have long casts. If a stack overlaps, resolve the stack first.

Between bosses 2 and 3: large pulls are possible.

Boss 3: Hermes

Upright edge sigils fire lines, leaving either the center or corners safe. After meteors land, sigils attack twice from two directions. Hide behind an uncracked meteor: cracked meteors withstand only one hit.

Interrupt True Bravery or the boss gains Damage Up.
789:
Vanaspati

Duty Support NPCs tend to choose the northern option when they can choose north or south.

Approach to boss 1: large pulls are possible; choose according to party capability.

Boss 1: Terminus Snatcher

When the floor darkens and mouths appear, stand by a closed mouth showing '...'. The left hand attacks left and the right hand attacks right; move opposite the raised hand.

The disorienting cry applies a status that only allows movement in the pointing finger's current direction. Work toward the safe region; about one second remains to adjust after the status ends.

Between bosses 1 and 2: large pulls are possible.

Boss 2: Terminus Wrecker

For knockback, avoid being pushed into edge orbs. For the large AoE, enter a water orb at the edge; each holds one player. Enter before the cast finishes because there is a slight delay.

Between bosses 2 and 3: killing one enemy spawns four more; treat them as part of the same pull.

Boss 3: Svarbhanu

The color cue appears as a screen overlay near its upper/lower edges, rather than only on the arena. Red circle: stand on blue floor. Blue inverted triangle: stand on red floor.

The second floor pattern includes knockback. Use immunity or account for its direction so you do not leave the arena. When the boss flies away, go east (3 o'clock) for the meteor sequence, dodging both meteors and circular ground AoEs.
790:
the Mothercrystal

Duty Support is recommended by the source. It grants an indomitable-will stack that can revive you at full HP after death.

The outer ring is lethal; never touch it.

After the weapon-change cast, read the weapons/color around Hydaelyn: red means move in, green means move out, pale blue/white means avoid front and sides because a cross AoE follows.

A red stack marker with two rotating orbs is specifically a two-tank stack. Tanks take it together.

After the first transition, destroy the crystals while handling proximity damage, stacks and spreads. Move toward the edge to reduce proximity damage.

Later, Crystallize combines with weapon changes. Ice means spreads; earth means a stack, with corresponding markers. Resolve the weapon's in/out positioning first, then the spread/stack.

For Parhelion, three sets of ring blades are thrown to the edges and later return through the center in the same order. Start in front of the third set, then move into the first set's cleared region once it returns to avoid sets two and three.

When lines extend outward from the middle, avoid their endpoints.

In the final phase, four waves appear: two point straight toward the center and divide the arena in a cross, leaving corner safe regions. The two angled waves cover three of those corners. Identify the remaining corner; following NPCs/experienced players can help if you cannot read it.

792:
the Dead Ends

The final boss's minion is untradeable. Throughout the dungeon, large pulls are possible and glowing objects beside the route provide background lore.

Boss 1: Caustic Grebuloff

Failed AoEs apply Necrosis, a lethal timed debuff. Healers must remove it with Esuna.

Wind messages and effects show the direction AoEs will move. Go upwind, toward the wind's origin. The second wind sequence starts with a donut: stay inside the target ring for that, then immediately move into the upwind gap.

Red inverted-triangle markers require sharing with another player; two or more overlapping players resolve them successfully.

Boss 2: Peacekeeper

Do not stand beneath the boss when it turns black. Small floating weapons emerge around its ring, with safe gaps between them. Numerous red AoEs follow ordered patterns: earlier ones resolve earlier. Avoid taking multiple hits and avoid crowding one another's escape routes.

When outer large AoEs combine with floating weapons, dodge the weapons first; the large AoEs resolve more slowly. The tank-targeted anti-personnel ray is a line, not just a single-target hit; everyone else stays clear of the tank's line.

Boss 3: Ra-la

For the four successive leaps, begin just outside the boundary of circles one and two. Once the first explodes, move into its cleared area without crossing the second circle.

After jumping to an edge, the boss fires a line and leaves golden butterflies. Read each butterfly's ground arrow to avoid its forward AoE. Being hit applies Doom, which is removed by healing the affected player to full HP.

A glowing wing signals a half-arena attack. If butterflies and a wing overlap, resolve the butterflies first, then the wing.
794:
Smileton

The design resembles Escher's Relativity, also an inspiration for Monument Valley. Routes between bosses have no special mechanics and allow large pulls.

Boss 1: Face

Large panels at the sides apply red frowning or blue smiling curses. The boss's tether shows which panel will attack. If you have red, take blue next; if blue, take red. Panels flip and can overlap spreads or knockbacks, so recheck them.

Three stacks of the same curse kill you. The narrow line between panel regions is also lethal; do not stand on it.

Boss 2: Frameworker

The forward leap travels about one target-ring diameter in front of the boss. Avoid that direction. Summoned drones create smaller copies that also leap forward: read the drones' facing and the arrows to predict the paths.

Boss 3: The Big Cheese

Conveyor arrows predict bomb positions: one arrow places the bomb toward the front; three arrows place it toward the rear. The usual safe start is near the boss on the three-arrow side.

Placed mining bombs can normally be ignored. If one occupies the required safe region, a tank can mitigate and deliberately trigger it; its blast is slightly larger than the visible bomb.

For the left/right arm cannon, move to the side named in the cast. If this overlaps conveyor bombs, resolve the bombs first and the arm cannon second.
796:
the Final Day

Avoid falling from the edge. In general, use gaps in edge hazards, move away from hazards appearing inside the arena, and spread marked attacks. Save the limit break for a tank.

After the opening raidwide, two planets appear. When the faster catches the slower, they explode at the slower planet's position; stay away from that position.

For Elenchos, an open glowing mouth means a central attack; a closed mouth with tears means side attacks.

Death's Embrace aims cones from the north at players. Spread to avoid overlapping cones, then avoid the feathers that fall afterward because they explode in circles.

Later planet collisions rewind and explode a second time at the same location. The second has a long animation and overlaps other mechanics. Two pairs later collide together: the boss's tether indicates which pair rewinds first and where its AoE will occur. Continue handling overlapping attacks.

After the adds, Ultimate Fate requires tank LB3 when the on-screen countdown reaches about five to four seconds. The boss uses Ultimate Fate again afterward.
800:
Asphodelos: The Fourth Circle

The perimeter is lethal. Setting the stage drops curtains and changes the arena when they rise. The central circular pit applies a very painful damage-over-time effect while you stand in it; leave immediately.

Elemental panels resolve differently:
- Lightning: lightning tiles explode and the center produces proximity damage. Stand at an edge outside lightning tiles.
- Water: water tiles explode and a central knockback occurs. Use knockback immunity, or start near the center with a path away from water tiles.
- Poison: spread marked AoEs while avoiding poison tiles.
- Fire: stack while avoiding fire tiles.

Towers display a crossed-out role icon: that role must not take that tower. Ensure every tower is occupied by an allowed role.

The directional shift attack places a sword or cloak at the named east/west/south/north edge. Sword: dodge to either side of that marker. Cloak: stand in front of the marker for its knockback.

Blood collection creates eight tethered orbs with crossed-out role icons. Take only orbs allowed for your role. Each player may take at most two; taking three applies Doom. Later mechanics repeat or combine these patterns.

802:
the Dark Inside

The opening reduces everyone's HP to 1. Gather for healing. The tankbuster is an AoE; everyone else stays away from the tank.

When the boss tethers an edge, a blue triangle indicates an isosceles-triangle attack with its point at that edge and its base opposite. Stand near the tethered edge, beside its point. A pink square instead attacks the tethered half; move to the opposite half.

Summoned behemoths produce circles and edge snakes produce lines. The first set gives plenty of time to inspect them. Healer stack markers hit repeatedly; mitigate and remain stacked.

For arena rotation, the floor turns clockwise or counterclockwise as indicated, while your character stays in place. Predict where the hazards will rotate and stand where the final layout will be safe.

Green totems fire lines in appearance order. Start by the later totem, then move into the first line's cleared area after it resolves. When the boss moves to a diagonal corner for a very wide dive, use an adjacent corner.

After the boss rises, star charts appear on three sides in succession. Each represents a 3-by-3 arena grid: starred cells explode. Resolve three successive patterns. Check the center first; if unsafe, inspect either lower chart corner. Facing the chart, its lower-left corresponds to your front-left and its lower-right to your front-right.

The boss continues auto-attacking while you handle charts. Healers can maintain a tank regen or single-target shield.

806:
Asphodelos: The Third Circle

The perimeter is lethal.

Read the conjured fireballs: one huge ball means move to the edge. A ring of small balls means watch the successive floor circles from the center; move to the right of the first circle, at the second circle's position, to avoid the later explosions.

The tankbuster is an AoE. Non-tanks stay clear of tanks.

Darkened Fire creates four small flames and marks four players with white circles. Use those circles to hit the flames; one circle can cover two. Do not miss a flame, even if covering it requires taking extra damage, because untouched flames cast a powerful attack.

Left/right wing attacks hit the named side. When the boss takes off and dives through the middle, use the sides. Later dives add spreads: divide between both sides, since at most five players fit safely on one side.

After the first dive, both tanks enable stance and take their small birds to the edges. Another pair spawns after the first dies. Keep all four birds from both waves outside other birds' circles or the subsequent raidwide becomes much stronger.

Later transformed birds attack the off-tank. Keep off-tank stance active and heal both tanks. If a tank dies, raise promptly and re-establish second enmity so a DPS is not hit.

Thin advancing flames converge into a cross, then explode as a much wider cross. Later this overlaps Darkened Fire: wait until the ground flames resolve, then move promptly to cover every dark flame. Again, covering flames takes priority over avoiding all extra damage.

Remaining mechanics repeat in combinations.

Approach to boss 1: two sections allow wall-to-wall pulls.

Boss 1: Lyngbakr

After the opening raidwide, the boss turns and casts a frontal half-arena breath. Move behind it. Small ice chunks produce circles roughly one boss diameter wide; the next large ice chunks produce circles about twice that size. Stacks/spreads follow the half-arena attack. The last ice pattern mixes both sizes: small chunks explode first, then large ones.

Between bosses 1 and 2: each section permits a large pull.

Boss 2: Arkas

Dodge the telegraphs. After the boss jumps to the edge, purple lines appear; their actual width is slightly greater than the preliminary markings. Tanks/melee should choose a wide gap. Once the dark-purple actual telegraph appears, about one second remains to adjust. The later arena is smaller and attacks resolve faster, but no new mechanic is added.

Between bosses 2 and 3: stop and clear enemies before each bridge.

Boss 3: Octomammoth

The arena is five connected circular platforms. For the tentacle slam, choose a platform without tentacles inside or outside it. For water attacks with blue circles on the platforms, stand at a connection between two platforms.

The breath attacks the boss's front half. Move along the target ring toward the side/rear; the small side arrows on the ring mark the front/rear boundary.

Telekinesis tethers edge rocks to platforms. Choose an untethered platform. A later tentacle/breath overlap may leave only a quarter of one platform safe, possibly within melee range. Read both attacks carefully.
823:
the Lunar Subterrane

Approach to boss 1: no special mechanics; large pulls are possible.

Boss 1: Dark Elf

The arena is a 4-by-4 grid. Purple staves attack their full row and column in a cross, initially two staves and later three. From the second occurrence, staves disappear before the cross cast, so remember the safe tiles. Being hit applies Doom; healers remove it with Esuna.

Blue-square and purple-triangle floor patterns accompany a matching pattern on the boss. The matching tiles explode: stand on the other pattern.

Between bosses 1 and 2

Large pulls are possible. Large enemies' wide AoEs can be stopped with stuns, but watch stun resistance from a white mage's Holy.

Boss 2: Damcyan Antlion

Landslip forces everyone about half an arena in the floor arrows' direction when its cast ends.

For the marching charge, read the red path and the two pillars it crosses. After the charge, Landslip moves the party, then those pillars fall immediately. Pillars have red exclamation marks while the path is shown; alternatively, inspect the missing/broken portions of side pillars during Landslip to choose a safe landing.

The stack leaves quicksand. Leave it promptly.

Between bosses 2 and 3: enemy casts can be stopped with stuns.

Boss 3: Durante

The double spiral attack shows two successive spiral patterns, then executes them in order. Dodge both. Purple orbs explode with a radius larger than the boss's target ring; stay away.

Later the boss splits orbs into two. Arrows show their travel directions before the resulting circular explosions. From the third set, five orbs leave only about one-ninth of the arena safe. Find the three with identical split directions: if one of those three is isolated from the others, use that orb's original position; otherwise use the middle one's position.

After the line stack and charge to an edge, the boss uses a roughly 150-degree inward cone. Stay close to its safe side. Giant claws signal a very wide line along their alignment; dodge to either side. A large orb tethered to a landing point makes an arena-diameter blast: move to the far edge away from its landing point.
824:
Worqor Zormor

Approach to boss 1: no special mechanics; enemies can be stunned.

Boss 1: Ryoqor Terteh

Small snow spirits attack a quarter-arena cone along their arrows. The boss freezes two, delaying their attacks. Start in front of a frozen spirit; once the unfrozen spirits attack, cross to the cleared side.

Large snow spirits instead attack circles around themselves. Again, two are frozen and delayed. Stand between their tethers, then cross through the boss after the other two attack.

Two waves of edge snowballs fire lines across the arena. Spread while dodging because individual markers overlap the lines.

The last set has four large and four small spirits, with four delayed. Start between tethered large spirits and read the small spirit between them: stand in front if it is tethered, behind if not. After the first hits, cross through the boss into the cleared safe area.

Between bosses 1 and 2

The stairs after the boss make a 180-degree turn. After the first upward transfer, moving forward-left against the cliff can enter the next transfer sooner. If you miss it, simply wait a moment.

Boss 2: Kahderyor

After the opening raidwide, shared towers leave crystals. Wind plus a donut requires gathering within the crystals; earth plus markers requires spreading away from them. Both occur, in variable order.

Three later line AoEs leave three crystal strips. Green wind: gather on a crystal (or far enough beyond it) for the donuts. Yellow earth: separate from one another and stay away from crystals; the earth area is large.

Crystallizing markers bind everyone. Stand close to the boss without overlapping so cleaving attacks can help break crystals. Break them within 21 seconds or the trapped players die.

Stone circle/wind donut casts also have a shrinking black eye indicator. Dodge the in/out AoE while looking away from the boss.

Between bosses 2 and 3: dodge the frequent AoEs; otherwise no special mechanics.

Boss 3: Gurfurlur

Red slabs create sequential AoEs centered on their positions. Blue slabs knock the whole party away from their edge for nearly three floor tiles. The line stack hits three times; do not leave early.

When the boss charges in the center, intercept the blue orbs moving toward it. Caught orbs grant player Damage Up; missed orbs buff the boss instead.

After the transition, green slabs cause a half-arena knockback. Edge whirlwinds then travel straight with a second knockback; immunity works. The final red/blue combination requires landing on the four tiles nearest the red slab, then spreading.
825:
Origenics

Readable files appear throughout. Use Duty Support if you want time to read them.

Approach to boss 1

Large enemies make pulls fairly painful and difficult to hit with AoEs. Choose pull size carefully.

Boss 1: Herpekaris

Two poison orbs drop after the opening raidwide. Watch which foot the boss raises to stomp one: its splash covers roughly half the arena, so use the other half. The boss returns to the center and shows three successive AoEs, then executes them in order. Later poison splashes are larger; move farther toward the safe edge.

Between bosses 1 and 2

Large pulls are possible. The later flying units use wide donuts and cannot be stunned; tanks/melee must dodge them.

Boss 2: Deceiver

Its swinging arms attack opposite diagonal quarters: front-left/rear-right or front-right/rear-left. Avoid both indicated quarters.

Support modules summon northern soldiers. Pixelated/glitching soldiers are illusions, and their lanes are safe. The real soldiers become attackable afterward; tanks pick them up.

Turrets appear east/west. Glitching turrets are fake, so their lines are safe. After one side fires, four new turrets appear opposite; read them again.

For the boss's edge knockback, align from the center toward a real turret. The turret stops your movement safely.

Between bosses 2 and 3

Large pulls are possible, but the last mechanical turtle has high HP and large AoEs. Clear the other enemies first. A healer's Repose can stop its stomp cast.

Boss 3: Ambrose the Undeparted

The suppressing attack hits the front half: watch its facing and move behind. When it jumps north and rattles side cages, use the third of the arena with no shaking cage on either side. Adds emerge afterward; tanks collect them.

Telekinetic Force divides the floor into four sections with directional knockback arrows. Later the version includes an immediate frontal half-arena attack after the knockback. Choose a section that sends you behind the boss.

The boss later throws a lightning spear from the edge. Dodge the red path markings, and do not stand in front when it retrieves the spear.
826:
Ihuykatumu

Approach to boss 1: enemies are fought on the moving route/platform; tanks establish enmity promptly.

Boss 1: Prime Punutiy

The frontal cone after its jump persists; do not return to the front early. Dodge the subsequent many AoEs; tanks/healers can help with shields. The final circular safe region gives ample time to reach it.

Four adds tether players for AoEs. Spread according to the telegraphs without aiming through teammates. For successive inner-circle then outer-ring attacks, start outside the circle and move beneath the boss between the hits.

Between bosses 1 and 2

Large pulls are possible. Upstairs, mimic blobs transform into party members. Keep moving during the transformation; they catch up afterward. Tanks should promptly pick them up to protect their targets.

Boss 2: Drowsie

Tentacles fire straight to the edge along their arrows, with lines two to three times wider than the arrow symbols. They later rotate and enlarge before striking again; avoid the wider lines or mitigate if caught. Immediately after the second slam, move behind the boss for its large cone.

When it jumps to the edge and spits many adds, group briefly so the tank can collect them, then dodge the marked circles.

Between bosses 2 and 3: no special mechanics; large pulls are possible.

Boss 3: Apollyon

After swallowing three adds, the boss jumps three times then fires a huge line from the edge. Melee should not charge in prematurely.

Small ground circles leave two purple sources of windmill-shaped triangular AoEs. Start near the first safe region, then move to the second between their hits.

After eating a sandworm, the boss uses a tankbuster, leaves a circular safe region and jumps to the edge. When wind appears within that circle, immediately move behind the boss to avoid the next large attack.

A whirlwind then moves across the arena with eight line indicators and fires along them after traveling. Distance makes the lines easier to dodge; melee may follow behind the whirlwind. Healers mitigate and restore health.
827:
Alexandria

The three scenes are all on the same map. The first two routes have no special mechanics; the final route allows large pulls.

Boss 1: Antivirus X

The boss is stationary and has no positional requirements. Learn its opening frontal and side cones for later combinations.

Five circle/cross symbols light up in sequence. Circle: stand inside. Cross: its full length and width become a cross AoE, so use a diagonal gap. The five attacks resolve quickly: move to the next safe spot as soon as the previous animation starts.

The tank's marked hit belongs away from the party; everyone else stacks. From the second circle/cross sequence, cone attacks resolve with the second and fifth symbols. Handle both. If unsure, one failed cone may be survivable, but multiple hits are dangerous; healers can mitigate.

The exit is at the room's northwest corner.

Boss 2: Amalgam

After a raidwide, small orbs trace a diagonal path from the center, turn at an arena corner and enclose a triangular danger region. Move to the opposite region.

Concentrated discharge attacks a central line, safe at the sides. Split discharge attacks side lines, safe in the center. Telegraphs are bright purple rather than yellow.

From the second triangle, three northern electrical orbs fire lines simultaneously with the triangle. Find a position safe from both. Resolve any spread markers afterward.

Boss 3: Eliminator

The slash attacks the weapon's left/right half. Move opposite it. Reconfiguration changes the weapon to the other hand and attacks the other half.

Subroutines move back-mounted hands to an edge to fire lines. Avoid both the hand lines and the half-arena slash. A later subroutine creates spotlights: stand inside a spotlight while also avoiding the slash, then spread.

After a stack, the boss vanishes and six lightning rods appear. Kill them promptly while continuing to handle spotlights, edge hands, lines and stacks.

After the transition, a huge blue circle causes long knockback. Stand just outside its edge on the side nearer the center; entering it is lethal. Immediately adjust for the following marked line AoEs.

The purge sequence produces four pairs of purple lines that slowly turn red, then fire wide line attacks. Watch and keep moving between them. If necessary, taking one may be survivable with mitigation/healing; avoid several.
829:
the Skydeep Cenote

The routes have no unusual mechanics; fight enemies and dodge telegraphs normally.

Boss 1: Feather Ray

The troublesome-tail cast applies a status that makes its target repeat the boss's attack when the overhead timer ends. Aim your repeated attack away from teammates. Dodge the boss's bubbles.

Medium bubbles are carried one space in the wave's indicated direction before exploding. Identify the current bubble-free safe spot, then stand one bubble-position downstream so that safe spot moves onto you. Later bubble volleys combine with the repeat status and create many more bubbles.

Boss 2: Firearms

The boss jumps to an edge and fires a line into a mirror. The reflection hits an orb across the arena, causing an enormous blast with a radius nearly the arena's width. Stay close to the boss at its edge. A brief delay between the line and orb explosion allows adjustment.

Back in the center, it activates two floor tiles and their horizontal/vertical neighbors. Use a clear tile. Later, the laser reflects through two mirrors, and three activated tiles leave only one safe tile.

Boss 3: Maulskull

The boss remains at the edge and has no positional requirements. Its charging fists strike half the arena in glow order: step across the middle between punches.

For the huge blue circle at the front, start just outside its edge and account for radial knockback. Avoid starting at the far sides, which can push you off.

When the boss retreats to charge, three sets of circles appear, followed by a green-arrow wide line. Dodge around the center. The forward tower hits three times; remain until all hits finish.

The second knockback combines with left/right punches. Land on the first safe side, then immediately cross the middle for the second punch. The final two knockbacks originate in the rear half and are followed by spreads/stacks. Keep enough separation without scattering too far to resolve the next mechanic.
830:
the Porta Decumana

- Titan: punches and quicksand; Ultima also repeats the punches. Dodge the telegraphs.
- Ifrit: advancing ground fire, sometimes after knockback. Return toward the center promptly after being pushed.
- Garuda: wind-eye hazards and large AoEs. Find a safe region near the center outside both.

After the primal phases, a cutscene leads to phase 2. Early lasers first project green lines onto the floor, then detonate; stay clear.

Other mechanics:
- Aetheric Boom: four orbs form two tethered pairs and approach one another. Intercept one orb per pair; its partner vanishes automatically. Contact causes a small AoE, but allowing a pair to collide causes raidwide damage.
- The siege cannon fires a frontal line as wide as the boss. Move to its sides/rear during the cast or charging animation. This often combines with stacks/gathering mechanics.
- Four corner impact markers: the center minimizes proximity damage.

Frequent AoEs and repeated damage require steady healing. Tanks and DPS should help with party mitigation.

At very low HP, the boss returns to the center for enrage. NPCs grant a damage buff; wait for it before using major damage attacks.
831:
Vanguard

Approach to boss 1

Motorcycles charge along the route. Run through a gap and group them with the three farther inside; tanks maintain enmity.

Boss 1: Vanguard Commander R8

High-speed movement shows a red path and one raised arm. The boss follows the path to the edge, then circles the arena, attacking on its raised-arm side throughout. Choose the inside or outside of its loop accordingly; damage resolves on animation.

When a squad is summoned, one row of enemies means line charges with gaps between them. Enemies around the perimeter instead explode in circles; use a corner. The third set combines charges from two directions with spreads. For the fourth, start in a corner and then move to the middle.

Between bosses 1 and 2

Floating weapons only establish enmity after firing their line AoE; tanks can collect them afterward while moving. Donut enemies can be stopped with Low Blow if needed.

Boss 2: Protector

Dodge the yellow circles during its barrage. After electrical grids appear, the rotating cannon attacks front/rear while turning. Follow its rotation while avoiding both grids and floor AoEs. You can pass beneath the boss when no yellow circle occupies it.

Acceleration Bomb requires stopping movement/actions, including auto-attacks, when its timer expires. Position out of nearby floor AoEs beforehand. The final barrage overlaps electrical grids; tanks/healers can add mitigation for the chaotic sequence.

Between bosses 2 and 3: collect the stationary artillery after their AoEs finish, as before.

Boss 3: Zander the Snakeskinner

The soul-blade line leaves a widening telegraph and expands into a half-arena attack after several seconds. This occurs successively in four directions with enough time to dodge calmly.

After being defeated, the boss revives at full HP. When it moves to the edge and S-shaped lines appear, go toward its position, to the half near the first orb without a curved path. Melee can follow behind the boss, but not in front.

The front/rear tail-blade attacks combine a line with a frontal/rear half-arena hit. Read the cast name. The line then expands into another half-arena attack; resolve the sequence without rushing.
832:
Worqor Lar Dor

This alliance raid is generally straightforward.

## First boss: Nophica
During the terrain-dependent attack, flowers indicate a point-blank circular AOE: move away. Grass indicates a donut AOE: move close to the boss.

The forced-movement debuff moves you for two seconds when its countdown expires. It always overlaps the terrain attack. Watch the terrain, your movement direction and the debuff's remaining time so the forced movement carries you to safety.

When yellow and blue circles and pillars appear, watch the shrinking effect above the pillars. Each pillar attacks when its shrinking circle reaches its smallest size. Stand in the floor circle matching that pillar's color.

## Second bosses: Althyk and Nymeia
The tanks should separate the bosses to break their proximity tether. Their HP is linked, so either can be attacked; focusing Nymeia generally makes her mechanics easier to follow.

Nymeia deals cards for either the attraction mechanic or the fire/ice mechanic. A single pull uses one of those sets, rather than both.

For the attraction cards, players with the normal pink/green effect must look away from Nymeia when the timer expires. Players with the reversed attraction effect must face her. The boss displays a question-mark eye marker.

For the fire/ice cards, stay still when the normal effect expires. With the reversed effect, keep moving as it expires; jumping or moving from side to side works.

After Althyk's raidwide attack, dark strips appear on the floor. If Nymeia is casting the water attack, stay outside the dark strips and spread for the markers. For the increased-gravity mechanic, stand inside a dark strip; otherwise the attack inflicts extra damage and vulnerability.

When a water-wave line with arrows appears across the center, start beside it. As soon as its first AOE resolves, move into the center to avoid the outward-expanding lines.

Both tanks must share the stacking tankbuster. The off-tank should join the tank holding the boss.

Three knockback pillars are marked with one, two and three diamonds. Start near the first pillar, slightly toward the second. After the first knockback, adjust to be knocked toward the third pillar; after the next knockback, adjust again to remain on the arena.

Althyk can accelerate the cards or the knockback pillars. A tethered pillar resolves its knockback first, so watch the tethers rather than assuming the ordinary order.

## Third boss: Halone
After the opening raidwide, Halone returns to the center and shows four AOE telegraphs in sequence. Stand near their boundaries and move to avoid them in order. They resolve quickly. If you cannot dodge everything, taking one is safer than taking several.

Three towers appear. The usual alliance assignment is A at the northwest tower, C at the northeast tower and B at the southern tower. If you cannot reach your own alliance's tower, enter the nearest one; ensure the towers are soaked.

When red circles gather around Halone, watch where they finally converge and disappear. She attacks that direction with a 180-degree AOE.

Two sets of golden weapons outside the arena each attack half of the floor. Their overlap leaves only one quarter safe.

The expanding and contracting ring attacks resolve as sequential donut AOEs. Follow the floor telegraphs; one sequence moves inward and the other outward.

During the three-spears phase, attack the spear assigned to your alliance while staying in the safe floor areas. A central spear also fires a rotating line AOE. Watch its rotation arrow and stand on the opposite side.

## Final boss: Menphina
A moon appears at the edge of the arena. When it becomes full, it fires an extremely wide line AOE. Move clear; the floor lines help show its width.

The tankbuster is a line attack. Tanks should position it away from the group.

Menphina later jumps to three large circular AOEs. Follow her between the jumps. Immediately after the third jump, move close to avoid the following donut attack.

Four smaller moons appear: two new moons, which are dark, and two half-lit moons. They all become full. Start in the new-moon areas, then move into the half-moon areas after those attacks resolve.

Handle the spread markers during the add phase.

Menphina then summons Dalamud. The wolf attacks half of the arena while Menphina performs her own mechanics. Combine their safe areas calmly. A quick clear avoids the more complicated overlaps; if damage is low, healers may want to retain their limit break for recovery.

When a head appears above each player, move away from your current position.

The boss also uses floor AOEs while the enemies are charging. Dodge both together. A gold arrow marks a chasing AOE: keep moving and do not lead it through other players.

- If one enemy enters an inner cup and the other an outer cup, with their positions forming a right angle around the arena center, the safe area remains roughly the same; stand closer to the edge.

The boss jumps to the edge and strikes a pillar with its horn, creating radial AOEs. Dodge them in the order they appear. It then marks a landing point: move away from that point toward the arena's edge. After the pillar falls, further line AOEs follow.

The boss later moves to the edge and begins charging while adds also charge in the arena. Everyone should switch targets and defeat the adds.

## First boss to the second boss
The enemies can be pulled together to the end of the passage. There are many of them, so the tank should ensure none are left attacking other players.

## Second boss: Overseer Kanilokka
After the opening tankbuster, numerous donut AOEs appear. Dodge them in their appearance order and avoid taking several hits together.

When the arena becomes dark red, dodge the floor AOEs first. Spread markers require space: move far enough apart to leave room for your teammates.

When a rotating finger appears above your head, pressing any movement direction makes you move in the direction the finger points. Some floor areas become safe while a proximity attack is marked. Carefully move toward the edge. If judging the finger's direction is difficult, tap movement repeatedly to slow its rotation. Tanks and healers can provide extra mitigation to players who cannot reach the edge.

The final stack overlaps floor AOEs. Everyone should move as close to the boss as possible, but does not need to stand at exactly the same point: the stack's area is approximately the size of the boss's targeting circle.

## Second boss to the final boss
There are no special mechanics to note.

## Final boss: Lunipyati
The repeated claw attack hits the front half of the arena. Continue avoiding the boss's front throughout the sequence.

Red arrows mark paths with AOEs at both their starting and ending points. Avoid all of them. The following spread resolves after the arrow sequence ends, so wait for the other effects to disappear before spreading.

Glowing spiral lines produce sequential circular AOEs along their paths. Melee players need a gap spanning two lines to remain in range; ranged players can use any suitable gap near the edge.

For the final long spiral extending from the boss to the edge, begin near the edge. Once the central AOE appears, immediately move beneath the boss to avoid the outer AOEs.

During the digging cast, the central floor cracks. Reach the intact outer ring before the cast finishes. The center becomes a hole, and falling in defeats you instantly.

When the boss jumps to the edge, first move away from it for the proximity attack. Sequential circular AOEs then expand from its position. Run against their direction of travel back toward the boss. It immediately jumps away and repeats the frontal claw attack: get behind it again, then handle the final spread or stack.

The floor does not return after the fight. Falling into the hole after combat is over has no encounter mechanic to resolve.

## Second boss: Soldier S0
When the boss raises its blade, several images appear and tether together before disappearing one by one. Only the final image performs the half-arena cleave. The first sequence follows a clockwise or counterclockwise chain: trace it to find the final image's safe side.

The boss jumps to the center and tethers to turrets at the edge. Their two half-arena attacks leave one quarter safe. Four players also receive cone markers; separate them toward the sides.

The final excavation-machine enemy uses a line charge followed by a frontal ray. Stun the charge with Low Blow to interrupt the cast and make the sequence easier to avoid.

## Final boss: Valia Pira
The boss remains in the center but rotates.

When two red orbs and two purple lines appear, purple blocks travel along the lines. A block hitting a red orb causes AOEs along that orb's row and column. The blocks do not necessarily start together, so watch their order. Ranged players can also stand in a position sharing neither a row nor a column with a red orb.

Activated turrets attack their entire rows. Move out of those rows.

The fixed cones and player-targeted cones widen. The smallest gaps are not safe; medium gaps fit one player and the largest gaps fit two. Spread accordingly.

The frontal electrical attack hits half of the arena. Move behind the boss.

When purple lines and red orbs return, one orb is tethered to a pale pink position. Treat the pink position as that orb's actual location when predicting its row and column attacks.

The final overlap combines turrets with three red orbs, including a moving orb. Watch the sequence calmly. If a mistake is unavoidable, taking one attack is safer than taking several.

The boss uses knockbacks from fixed points and circular floor AOEs. It later adds a visual interference effect, but the real attack areas and their resolution order do not change. Remember the original pattern.

The final sequence combines knockbacks and circles. If you lose track, stand in a safe gap between the circles and use knockback immunity. Avoid being hit by several circles or knocked to the edge.

## Second encounter: Executioners' memories
Four enemies each tether to a different player and give that player a corresponding effect. Initially, you can attack only the enemy tethered to you. Each player is then pulled into their enemy's ring. If you are defeated during the duel, you are pulled back into it a few seconds after being resurrected.

The shared mechanics are:
- Four staggered sets of blades appear at the edges and fire line AOEs.
- Four staggered sets of electrical lines move slowly across the floor. After they pass the midpoint, point-blank or donut AOEs follow.
- Three landing markers are quickly followed by iron balls. Immediately move to the edge between adjacent balls; there is little time to react.
- The continuous-execution sequence combines blades, iron balls, blades, then a point-blank or donut attack. Use personal mitigation and healing if necessary, and minimize the number of hits you take.

Each role also has a separate responsibility:
- Tank: interrupt the projectile cast with Interject. Use substantial mitigation for the heavy combo tankbuster, since the healer may be occupied elsewhere.
- Healer: use Esuna on yourself to remove Doom.
- DPS: destroy the burning torture device outside the arena while continuing to dodge the floor mechanics. Otherwise, its damage-over-time effect intensifies and can quickly become fatal.

After defeating your own enemy, you can help attack the others. Melee players must still avoid attacks inside another player's ring. Ranged players can assist from outside it.

## Second encounter to the final boss
Two soldiers in the final group cast circular AOEs. Stun or interrupt those casts to make the pull easier.

## Final boss: Others' memories
When machines at the edge tether to figures in the arena, the tethers mark extremely wide line AOEs. Find an untethered area. After the first set resolves, immediately move into an intersection of its former lines to avoid the second set. The source's illustration marks the danger areas in purple and example positions in green.

When several groups of figures appear, larger groups produce larger AOEs. Find a lone figure and move near it.

When the boss slowly raises one hand and the charging message appears, it attacks the half of the arena corresponding to that raised hand. Move to the other half.

When figures appear with a blue circle in the center, do not stand inside the blue circle: it deals extremely heavy damage. It also produces a knockback. Position yourself so the knockback sends you toward a lone figure.

When two groups of figures run away, their directions mark two very wide line AOEs. One is parallel to an arena edge and the other diagonal. Each covers roughly half of the arena. Positions tight against the ends of the parallel line are safe; one side has less space, so stay close to the edge. Ranged players can also use the area outside the diagonal line.
